detail.check: Repeat the frozen matched-line sampler, recover the same whole-line crops from the Yale IIIF manifest, and give randomized unlabeled crop panels to additional readers. Extend whole-line segmentation to the unsupported layouts. Compare the signed within-line width difference across quires with the least reliable lines retained as unresolved, and measure how often alternative alignments reverse the effect.
interpretation: Both masked readers matched all four edges within 20 native pixels for 14 of the 18 initial crops, spanning ten quires. The certain gap is larger in each measured pair. The equal-quire contrast is +3.75 pixels rescaled to a 700-pixel page. Excluding pages from the original direct ink study leaves 12 of 12 positive cases with an equal-quire contrast of +3.42 pixels. Both left-to-right label orientations give the same direction.

The exception log is part of the result. Two initially mapped photographs do not provide reliable matches to the complete reference row. One crop cuts off the right glyph and one repeated sequence received discrepant placements. Expanded-crop recovery and a tie-breaking reader are reported separately. The alternate locators broaden coverage across compound leaves while keeping the sample small and conditional on visually identifiable glyphs.

All 25 resolved comparisons were wider at the period across 15 marked quire groups. This combines the primary sample, nine supplemental whole-line matches and two recoveries. Only the explicitly specified 14 are used for the primary width estimate.

In the larger archived-pixel analysis, 99 of 121 exact-pair lines on 54 pages or panels favor the certain gap. The equal-quire mean difference is +0.269 threshold units with bootstrap interval [−0.757, +0.892]. An anomalous 242 px comma width at f35r.8 dominates one quire estimate, and our blind strip cannot safely verify the corresponding row. Equal-token-count cases alone have an equal-quire mean of −0.090, showing the dependence of the archive result on how its alignment branches contribute.

This documents the predicted physical spacing contrast in the identifiable same-glyph sample. The proportions cannot estimate the distribution of all spaces or establish the lexical status of either separator. Broad independent confirmation would require a larger set of reliably aligned image lines, especially at dense, interrupted, or heavily illustrated layouts.

primary_method.blinding: Four auxiliary image-model readers independently inspect overlapping groups of anonymous strips, so two readers cover each initial line. Each panel has a native pixel ruler and a detached reference in EVA-basic with every separator removed. Two randomized A and B markers in that reference indicate which stroke transitions to locate, without identifying their separator classes. The reference x positions are unrelated to the photograph. Give readers no physical word locations or separator categories. The panel ordering and marker labels use seed 104081551.
primary_method.companion_checks: The archive's initial folios are f7v, f14v, f23r, f39v, f42v and f56v. Repeat the primary result after excluding them. Independently try one wider crop for the clipped right edge and one additional reader for an exact repeated-glyph alignment disagreement. Keep these recovery measurements outside the primary tally. A further alternative-layout check uses whole-line locators cross-registered with old archive boxes and normal-light Yale crops, without giving the optical readers either target coordinates or separator classes. The whole-canvas width conversion compresses units differently on wide foldouts, so use native edges and the within-line sign for the supplemental comparison.
primary_method.measurement: Each reader matches the full unspaced sequence by inspection, then records the left glyph's rightmost horizontal ink extent and the right glyph's leftmost extent. Use max(0,right-left-1) native pixels so touching or overlapping glyph envelopes contribute zero. Compare the same-line difference after averaging the two estimates and multiplying by 700 divided by native canvas width. Require all four estimated endpoints to agree between readers within 20 pixels; show a 10-pixel sensitivity. Quire means receive equal weight. Repeat the quire-cluster bootstrap 4,000 times with fixed seed 20261126. This is a small convenience sample among eligible lines with measurable geometry, and the intervals are descriptive.
primary_method.sampling: Use the public practice training set. Retain paragraph lines composed entirely of lowercase EVA and literal comma or period after deleting edge paragraph markers. In EVA-basic select a period and a comma on the same line with exactly the same ordered glyph pair. The frozen 27 cases use distinct numbered leaves. Twelve quires contribute two cases of at most two separator ordinals apart and three additional eligible quires contribute one case with a cap of two or four ordinals. Optimize opposite left-to-right label orientations, then ordinal distance and exact pair diversity, with SHA256-seeded tie breaks. The original selection had 16 period-left and 11 period-right cases.
primary_method.whole_line_localization: Use only the S45 image-native baselines and polygons from unique 1:1 row matches, giving 18 lines from ten quires. The existing whole-line correspondence uses continuous glyph counts, without specifying where either sampled separator lies. Exclude seven compound or foldout loci that lack the corresponding S45 crop, and two loci with non-1:1 matches. Native photographs are displayed as padded whole-line strips, retaining useful context for ambiguous tall strokes. There are no imported boundaries or word boxes on the displayed ink.

detail.prior_evidence: Rozanova and Temerev found a strong distinction using Voynichese token boxes. Their direct pixel pilot measures the physical ink but uses those same boxes to locate gaps on six folios. It retains 265 certain and 21 uncertain gaps, giving a mean contrast of +1.84 pixels at 700 pixels page width. Its eighteen exact-pair comparisons were post hoc. The present spot audit matches both glyphs on the same line prospectively and gives the readers no inherited word boxes.

s47_reanalysis_method.comparison: Subtract uncertain width from certain width and divide by the published geometric threshold for that line. Report both pooled results and equally weighted quire means. Recompute descriptive percentile intervals with 4,000 quire resamples and seed 1947. Check orientation, proximity, quire exclusion and the alignment branches with equal or unequal detected versus transcribed token counts. The published table has 2,441 loci with emitted positions, including width-gate failures.
s47_reanalysis_method.independence_limit: S47 ink segmentation precedes transcription alignment, but its width at a separator depends on alignment to transcribed tokens. Some within-token distances are placed at proportional glyph offsets. Guarding on exact ordinal sequence and exact glyph pair leaves this dependency in place. The larger reanalysis tests robustness of the archived measurements and the small blind audit tests independence of the pixel edges.
s47_reanalysis_method.mapping: Read the published S47 positions on public scans. Read the pinned raw ZL paragraph lines using the strict clean-line rule. Reconstruct the entire ordinal sequence of periods, commas and internal positions with the S47 glyph segmentation (EVA-basic plus iiin, iin, in, iir, ir and ee). Require exact agreement to the observed row labels and lengths before transferring any glyph-pair identities. Drop lines with any missing width; use the nearest same-pair cross-class match per line, breaking ties by period ordinal, then comma ordinal. This additional filter avoids choosing gaps by magnitude.

sampling_record.glyph_convention: EVA-basic token-internal segmentation. Glyphs are indexed from zero in the concatenated segmented words. Raw EVA character offsets also start at zero and mark a point between characters.
sampling_record.selection: Two different numbered leaves per A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,M,N,S,T; distance ≤2. Optimize opposite dot/comma orientations, then summed distance, then distinct edge pairs, then seeded SHA-256 order. Add one in each I,O,Q in that order at caps 4,2,4; minimize orientation imbalance then distance then seeded SHA-256 order. IDs sorted by the same seeded hash.

Check orientation, proximity, quire exclusion and the alignment branches with equal or unequal detected versus transcribed token counts. The published table has 2,441 loci with emitted positions, including width-gate failures.
s47_reanalysis_method.independence_limit: S47 ink segmentation precedes transcription alignment, but its width at a separator depends on alignment to transcribed tokens. Some within-token distances are placed at proportional glyph offsets. Guarding on exact ordinal sequence and exact glyph pair leaves this dependency in place. The larger reanalysis tests robustness of the archived measurements and the small blind audit tests independence of the pixel edges.
s47_reanalysis_method.mapping: Read the published S47 positions on public scans. Read the pinned raw ZL paragraph lines using the strict clean-line rule. Reconstruct the entire ordinal sequence of periods, commas and internal positions with the S47 glyph segmentation (EVA-basic plus iiin, iin, in, iir, ir and ee). Require exact agreement to the observed row labels and lengths before transferring any glyph-pair identities. Drop lines with any missing width; use the nearest same-pair cross-class match per line, breaking ties by period ordinal, then comma ordinal. This additional filter avoids choosing gaps by magnitude.

sampling_record.glyph_convention: EVA-basic token-internal segmentation. Glyphs are indexed from zero in the concatenated segmented words. Raw EVA character offsets also start at zero and mark a point between characters.
sampling_record.selection: Two different numbered leaves per A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,M,N,S,T; distance ≤2. Optimize opposite dot/comma orientations, then summed distance, then distinct edge pairs, then seeded SHA-256 order. Add one in each I,O,Q in that order at caps 4,2,4; minimize orientation imbalance then distance then seeded SHA-256 order. IDs sorted by the same seeded hash.

findings: The complete result object from the recorded P-L1-007 script reproduced exactly, including all 72 planting conditions, three adjacency-preserving surrogates, public ZL/Takahashi partitions and twelve inherited line-chain controls. This replicates that implementation, not the authors' unpublished executable or their full-manuscript numerical results.

With word-boundary positions and candidate counts matched, full-pool replacement supports eight of twelve language/partition/contrast comparisons. The wrong-origin candidate has a lower loss in six and the genuine candidate in two, in both literal and prose modes. In four comparisons both candidates rank within 5%. These selected, shared-first-component contrasts do not estimate a population false-positive rate.

With exact previous glyph also matched, all 36 inherited planting conditions have identical X/Z scores despite different outgoing counts; thirteen meet support when counting all three replacement fractions. The tie follows from equal candidate frequency, equal incoming counts, and zero self-adjacency while proposed components A,B are held fixed. No term uses the right-context distribution of the candidate itself.

Separately written counting and loss code agrees with the inherited eight-rule vectors over 556316 triplet-by-convention evaluations in 32 text/convention conditions; the largest rule discrepancy is 3.3306690738754696e-16. All 176 tracked candidate rank decisions at the 5% threshold agree when the independent ranker includes floating-point ties.

At full matched-pool coverage, four additional fixed pairing seeds each reproduce six decoy wins and two genuine wins among eight supported word-position comparisons. Exact-left matching gives seven supported ties per seed. Across all five seed settings, all sixty exact-left trials have different outgoing counts and equal loss for X and Z. Seed settings were fixed in the audit script before running them; none was selected for its outcome.

A separately implemented first-order glyph line chain fitted only on public practice training lines, with six new seeds per edition, places m|i|d in the best 5% in all twelve emitted texts under both conventions. q|i|e passes in two of six ZL-trained and four of six Takahashi-trained texts. This generator emits one glyph at a time from a single transition table and never performs pair fusion. This is a public specificity control, not a new hidden-page generator submission.

For public evaluation q|i|e, the rarer member has one retained incoming context in each edition. Changing only the undefined-single-context Pearson loss from zero to one changes prose-mode rank from 0.04411764705882353 to 0.09627757352941177 in ZL and from 0.04388786764705882 to 0.09857536764705882 in Takahashi. The cutoff decision reverses. The zero-variance case with at least two contexts retains the inherited convention.
limitations: Public practice and reference partitions only; no hidden-page evaluation or scan adjudication was performed.
The full-support comparisons are a selected subset of twelve conditions. Planting seeds are not independent language samples and do not justify a significance estimate.
The 5% rank threshold is a ranking convention over candidate triplets, not a calibrated statistical p-value.
The fixed candidate triplets are investigated examples, not a search over all possible writing systems. Their low rank without fusion does not establish that manuscript glyphs are indivisible.
Printed/stated-rule differences and undefined Pearson cases prevent calling this an exact numerical reproduction of the original paper.

methods.independent_chain: Fit one character-transition count table per edition on public practice training paragraph lines. Sample initial glyphs from training starts; follow the table using sorted cumulative integer draws. At the last position disallow a space. Use public evaluation line lengths, join lines by one space, and never fuse glyphs. This boundary handling means stationarity applies to the shared internal table, not to initial/final positions.
methods.independent_implementation: Counts windows in a separate loop; uses integer incoming counts and Pearson raw sums, rather than the inherited centred probability vectors. Independently checks source offsets, word-boundary and previous-glyph signature equality. The inherited matcher and encoder are reused, so these are numerical and sampling-invariant checks rather than a completely separate planting implementation.
methods.loss_conventions: Weights (1,100,1,1,100,1,1,10). Zero an edge below 0.2% of either row or column. Relative glyph support >500/229431. Percentile includes ties over non-space eligible ordered triplets with candidate distinct from components. Literal mode uses matched mass for Rule 3 and (1-min(pA,pB))/max(p) for Rule 6; prose mode uses unmatched mass and 1-min(pA,pB)/max(p). methods.rank_ties: Independent ranks count all losses <= the candidate loss or numerically equal with rel_tol=abs_tol=1e-12. Loss-vector agreement is checked at rel_tol=abs_tol=1e-11. All tracked 5% decisions agree.
methods.reference_conditions: Pinned normalized English, Latin and Italian train/control blocks; up to 40000 characters, trimmed before the last partial word. Contrasts th/to and ea/er; en/es and pa/pe; ch/co and de/di. Candidate labels X,Z denote equal numbers of separated replacements. """Independent numerical audit of P-L1-007 on public practice/reference text.

The inherited script supplies the deterministic planting and line-chain generation.
This module recomputes the loss and rank from separately counted text windows.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import math
import random
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from itertools import product
from pathlib import Path

import original_triplet as original
from vs import corpus, refcorpus

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WEIGHTS = (1, 100, 1, 1, 100, 1, 1, 10)


class AuditScore:
    def __init__(self, text, single_loss=0):
        self.n = len(text)
        self.count = Counter()
        self.edges = Counter()
        self.row, self.col = Counter(), Counter()
        for i, ch in enumerate(text):
            self.count[ch] += 1
            if i:
                previous = text[i - 1]
                self.edges[previous, ch] += 1
                self.row[previous] += 1
                self.col[ch] += 1
        self.symbols = sorted(self.count)
        self.kept = {edge: n for edge, n in self.edges.items()
                     if n * 500 >= max(self.row[edge[0]], self.col[edge[1]])}
        self.p = {ch: n / self.n for ch, n in self.count.items()}
        self.max_p = max(self.count.values()) / self.n
        self.max_edge = max(self.kept.values()) / (self.n - 1)
        diagonal = [n / (self.n - 1) for (a, b), n in self.kept.items() if a == b]
        self.max_diagonal = max(diagonal) if diagonal else 1
        self.eligible = [ch for ch in self.symbols
                         if ch != ' ' and self.count[ch] * 229431 > 500 * self.n]
        self.single_loss = single_loss
        self.left = {}
        for c, a in product(self.symbols, repeat=2):
            rare, frequent = (c, a) if self.count[c] <= self.count[a] else (a, c)
            contexts = [s for s in self.symbols if (s, rare) in self.kept]
            u = [self.kept[s, rare] for s in contexts]
            v = [self.kept.get((s, frequent), 0) for s in contexts]
            if len(contexts) < 2:
                correlation_loss = single_loss if contexts else 0
            else:
                # Pearson via raw sums rather than the inherited centred vectors.
                n = len(u)
                covariance = n * sum(x * y for x, y in zip(u, v)) - sum(u) * sum(v)
                variance_u = n * sum(x * x for x in u) - sum(u) ** 2
                variance_v = n * sum(y * y for y in v) - sum(v) ** 2
                denominator = math.sqrt(variance_u * variance_v)
                correlation_loss = 1 - min(1, abs(covariance / denominator)) if denominator else 1
            common = sum(x for x, y in zip(u, v) if y) / (self.n - 1)
            uncommon = sum(x for x, y in zip(u, v) if not y) / (self.n - 1)
            self.left[c, a] = common, uncommon, correlation_loss

    def losses(self, c, a, b, version):
        pc, pa, pb = self.p[c], self.p[a], self.p[b]
        common, uncommon, pearson = self.left[c, a]
        probability = lambda edge: self.kept.get(edge, 0) / (self.n - 1)
        return (
            max(pc - max(pa, pb), 0) / self.max_p,
            probability((a, b)) / self.max_edge,
            common if version == 'literal' else uncommon,
            pearson,
            probability((c, c)) / self.max_diagonal,
            (1 - min(pa, pb)) / self.max_p if version == 'literal' else 1 - min(pa, pb) / self.max_p,
            pc / ((pa + pc) * (pb + pc)),
            int(a == b),
        )

    def total(self, triplet, version):
        return sum(w * loss for w, loss in zip(WEIGHTS, self.losses(*triplet, version)))


def verify_text(text, label, single_loss=0, tracked=()):
    audit = AuditScore(text, single_loss)
    inherited = original.Score(text, single_context_loss=single_loss)
    assert audit.eligible == inherited.alphabet
    errors = []
    for version in ('literal', 'prose'):
        checked = 0
        max_error = 0
        universe_losses = []
        for t in product(audit.eligible, repeat=3):
            if t[0] in t[1:]:
                continue
            checked += 1
            av, bv = audit.losses(*t, version), inherited.losses(*t, version)
            error = max(abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(av, bv))
            max_error = max(max_error, error)
            assert all(math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-11, abs_tol=1e-11) for x, y in zip(av, bv)), (label, t, av, bv)
            universe_losses.append(sum(w * x for w, x in zip(WEIGHTS, av)))
        ranks = {}
        inherited_rank = inherited.ranker(version)
        for t in tracked:
            if not all(ch in audit.count for ch in t):
                continue
            score = audit.total(t, version)
            # Include numerical ties, rather than breaking them by floating point round-off.
            rank = sum(x <= score or math.isclose(x, score, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-12)
                       for x in universe_losses) / len(universe_losses)
            previous = inherited_rank(t)
            ranks['|'.join(t)] = {'audit_rank_with_ties': rank, 'recorded_rank': previous['rank'],
                                  'same_5pct_decision': (rank <= .05) == (previous['rank'] <= .05)}
            assert ranks['|'.join(t)]['same_5pct_decision'], (label, t, ranks['|'.join(t)])
        errors.append({'version': version, 'triplets': checked, 'max_rule_absolute_error': max_error, 'tracked_ranks': ranks})
    return {'label': label, 'characters': len(text), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest(), 'audit': errors}


def main():
    output = {'audited_texts': [], 'matching_checks': [], 'seed_sensitivity': []}
    # Original contrast seeds, plus four fixed new seeds, chosen before this run.
    seeds = [9141, 137, 271, 409, 593]
    for language, contrasts in original.CONTRASTS.items():
        for partition, loader in [('train', refcorpus.train_text), ('control', refcorpus.control_text)]:
            text = ' ' + ' '.join(loader(language))[:40000].rsplit(' ', 1)[0] + ' '
            for index, (target, decoy) in enumerate(contrasts):
                for by_left in (False, True):
                    for seed in seeds:
                        actual_seed = seed + index if seed == 9141 else seed
                        pool = original.paired_positions(text, target, decoy, by_left, actual_seed)
                        encoded = original.encode(text, pool)
                        # Verify planting directly from source offsets, independently of the grouping code.
                        signature_x, signature_z = Counter(), Counter()
                        for i, j in pool:
                            assert text[i:i+2] == target and text[j:j+2] == decoy
                            signature = lambda k: (text[k-1] == ' ', text[k+2] == ' ', text[k-1] if by_left else '')
                            signature_x[signature(i)] += 1
                            signature_z[signature(j)] += 1
                        assert signature_x == signature_z
                        audit = AuditScore(encoded)
                        assert audit.count['X'] == audit.count['Z'] == len(pool)
                        incoming = sum(abs(audit.edges[s, 'X'] - audit.edges[s, 'Z']) for s in audit.symbols)
                        outgoing = sum(abs(audit.edges['X', s] - audit.edges['Z', s]) for s in audit.symbols)
                        eligible = 'X' in audit.eligible and 'Z' in audit.eligible
                        row = {'language': language, 'partition': partition, 'target': target, 'decoy': decoy,
                               'left_matched': by_left, 'seed': actual_seed, 'pairs': len(pool),
                               'eligible': eligible, 'incoming_L1': incoming, 'outgoing_L1': outgoing, 'scores': {}}
                        for version in ('literal', 'prose'):
                            x, z = audit.total(('X', *target), version), audit.total(('Z', *target), version)
                            row['scores'][version] = {'X': x, 'Z': z, 'difference_X_minus_Z': x-z}
                            if by_left:
                                assert incoming == 0 and math.isclose(x, z, abs_tol=1e-12)
                        output['seed_sensitivity'].append(row)
                        if seed == 9141:
                            label = f'{language}/{partition}/{target}-{decoy}/left={by_left}'
                            output['audited_texts'].append(verify_text(encoded, label, tracked=[('X', *target), ('Z', *target)]))
    for edition in ('zl', 'it'):
        for partition, pages in zip(('train', 'evaluation'), corpus.split_pages('practice', edition)):
            text = ' '.join(w for p in pages for ln in p.lines if ln.unit == 'P'
                            for w in ln.words if w.isascii() and w.isalpha())
            for single_loss in (0, 1):
                output['audited_texts'].append(verify_text(text, f'{edition}/{partition}/singleton={single_loss}', single_loss, original.DRAFT_TRIPLETS))
    output['independent_line_chain'] = independent_line_chain()
    (ROOT / 'audit.json').write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
    print(json.dumps({'audited_texts': len(output['audited_texts']), 'seed_conditions': len(output['seed_sensitivity'])}))


def independent_line_chain():
    """Fit a first-order table separately and emit glyphs without any pair fusion."""
    results = []
    for edition in ('zl', 'it'):
        training, evaluation = corpus.split_pages('practice', edition)
        clean = lambda pages: [' '.join(w for w in ln.words if w.isascii() and w.isalpha())
                               for p in pages for ln in p.lines if ln.unit == 'P']
        train = [ln for ln in clean(training) if ln]
        lengths = [len(ln) for ln in clean(evaluation) if ln]
        starts, transitions = Counter(ln[0] for ln in train), defaultdict(Counter)
        for line in train:
            for i in range(1, len(line)):
                transitions[line[i-1]][line[i]] += 1
        for seed in range(18710, 18716):
            rng = random.Random(seed)
            def draw(counts):
                # Sorted, cumulative integer sampling differs from the inherited expanded-list sampler.
                threshold = rng.randrange(sum(counts.values()))
                for symbol, count in sorted(counts.items()):
                    if threshold < count:
                        return symbol
                    threshold -= count
                raise AssertionError('invalid transition draw')
            lines = []
            for length in lengths:
                sequence = [draw(starts)]
                while len(sequence) < length:
                    options = transitions[sequence[-1]]
                    if len(sequence) == length - 1:
                        options = Counter({s: n for s, n in options.items() if s != ' '})
                    sequence.append(draw(options or starts))
                lines.append(''.join(sequence))
            text = ' '.join(lines)
            assert [len(s) for s in lines] == lengths and '  ' not in text
            calculator = AuditScore(text)
            row = {'edition': edition, 'seed': seed, 'characters': len(text),
                   'sha256': hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest(), 'ranks': {}}
            for version in ('literal', 'prose'):
                losses = [calculator.total(t, version) for t in product(calculator.eligible, repeat=3) if t[0] not in t[1:]]
                row['ranks'][version] = {}
                for t in original.DRAFT_TRIPLETS:
                    if not all(ch in calculator.p for ch in t):
                        continue
                    score = calculator.total(t, version)
                    rank = sum(x <= score or math.isclose(x, score, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-12) for x in losses) / len(losses)
                    row['ranks'][version]['|'.join(t)] = {'rank': rank, 'competing': all(ch in calculator.eligible for ch in t)}
            results.append(row)
    return results


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Contrasts th/to and ea/er; en/es and pa/pe; ch/co and de/di. Candidate labels X,Z denote equal numbers of separated replacements. Planting fractions 1/4, 1/2 and 1 of the matched pool, not of all target occurrences.

scripts.audit_triplet.py:
"""Independent numerical audit of P-L1-007 on public practice/reference text.

The inherited script supplies the deterministic planting and line-chain generation.
This module recomputes the loss and rank from separately counted text windows.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import math
import random
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from itertools import product
from pathlib import Path

import original_triplet as original
from vs import corpus, refcorpus

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WEIGHTS = (1, 100, 1, 1, 100, 1, 1, 10)


class AuditScore:
    def __init__(self, text, single_loss=0):
        self.n = len(text)
        self.count = Counter()
        self.edges = Counter()
        self.row, self.col = Counter(), Counter()
        for i, ch in enumerate(text):
            self.count[ch] += 1
            if i:
                previous = text[i - 1]
                self.edges[previous, ch] += 1
                self.row[previous] += 1
                self.col[ch] += 1
        self.symbols = sorted(self.count)
        self.kept = {edge: n for edge, n in self.edges.items()
                     if n * 500 >= max(self.row[edge[0]], self.col[edge[1]])}
        self.p = {ch: n / self.n for ch, n in self.count.items()}
        self.max_p = max(self.count.values()) / self.n
        self.max_edge = max(self.kept.values()) / (self.n - 1)
        diagonal = [n / (self.n - 1) for (a, b), n in self.kept.items() if a == b]
        self.max_diagonal = max(diagonal) if diagonal else 1
        self.eligible = [ch for ch in self.symbols
                         if ch != ' ' and self.count[ch] * 229431 > 500 * self.n]
        self.single_loss = single_loss
        self.left = {}
        for c, a in product(self.symbols, repeat=2):
            rare, frequent = (c, a) if self.count[c] <= self.count[a] else (a, c)
            contexts = [s for s in self.symbols if (s, rare) in self.kept]
            u = [self.kept[s, rare] for s in contexts]
            v = [self.kept.get((s, frequent), 0) for s in contexts]
            if len(contexts) < 2:
                correlation_loss = single_loss if contexts else 0
            else:
                # Pearson via raw sums rather than the inherited centred vectors.
                n = len(u)
                covariance = n * sum(x * y for x, y in zip(u, v)) - sum(u) * sum(v)
                variance_u = n * sum(x * x for x in u) - sum(u) ** 2
                variance_v = n * sum(y * y for y in v) - sum(v) ** 2
                denominator = math.sqrt(variance_u * variance_v)
                correlation_loss = 1 - min(1, abs(covariance / denominator)) if denominator else 1
            common = sum(x for x, y in zip(u, v) if y) / (self.n - 1)
            uncommon = sum(x for x, y in zip(u, v) if not y) / (self.n - 1)
            self.left[c, a] = common, uncommon, correlation_loss

    def losses(self, c, a, b, version):
        pc, pa, pb = self.p[c], self.p[a], self.p[b]
        common, uncommon, pearson = self.left[c, a]
        probability = lambda edge: self.kept.get(edge, 0) / (self.n - 1)
        return (
            max(pc - max(pa, pb), 0) / self.max_p,
            probability((a, b)) / self.max_edge,
            common if version == 'literal' else uncommon,
            pearson,
            probability((c, c)) / self.max_diagonal,
            (1 - min(pa, pb)) / self.max_p if version == 'literal' else 1 - min(pa, pb) / self.max_p,
            pc / ((pa + pc) * (pb + pc)),
            int(a == b),
        )

    def total(self, triplet, version):
        return sum(w * loss for w, loss in zip(WEIGHTS, self.losses(*triplet, version)))


def verify_text(text, label, single_loss=0, tracked=()):
    audit = AuditScore(text, single_loss)
    inherited = original.Score(text, single_context_loss=single_loss)
    assert audit.eligible == inherited.alphabet
    errors = []
    for version in ('literal', 'prose'):
        checked = 0
        max_error = 0
        universe_losses = []
        for t in product(audit.eligible, repeat=3):
            if t[0] in t[1:]:
                continue
            checked += 1
            av, bv = audit.losses(*t, version), inherited.losses(*t, version)
            error = max(abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(av, bv))
            max_error = max(max_error, error)
            assert all(math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=1e-11, abs_tol=1e-11) for x, y in zip(av, bv)), (label, t, av, bv)
            universe_losses.append(sum(w * x for w, x in zip(WEIGHTS, av)))
        ranks = {}
        inherited_rank = inherited.ranker(version)
        for t in tracked:
            if not all(ch in audit.count for ch in t):
                continue
            score = audit.total(t, version)
            # Include numerical ties, rather than breaking them by floating point round-off.
            rank = sum(x <= score or math.isclose(x, score, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-12)
                       for x in universe_losses) / len(universe_losses)
            previous = inherited_rank(t)
            ranks['|'.join(t)] = {'audit_rank_with_ties': rank, 'recorded_rank': previous['rank'],
                                  'same_5pct_decision': (rank <= .05) == (previous['rank'] <= .05)}
            assert ranks['|'.join(t)]['same_5pct_decision'], (label, t, ranks['|'.join(t)])
        errors.append({'version': version, 'triplets': checked, 'max_rule_absolute_error': max_error, 'tracked_ranks': ranks})
    return {'label': label, 'characters': len(text), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest(), 'audit': errors}


def main():
    output = {'audited_texts': [], 'matching_checks': [], 'seed_sensitivity': []}
    # Original contrast seeds, plus four fixed new seeds, chosen before this run.
    seeds = [9141, 137, 271, 409, 593]
    for language, contrasts in original.CONTRASTS.items():
        for partition, loader in [('train', refcorpus.train_text), ('control', refcorpus.control_text)]:
            text = ' ' + ' '.join(loader(language))[:40000].rsplit(' ', 1)[0] + ' '
            for index, (target, decoy) in enumerate(contrasts):
                for by_left in (False, True):
                    for seed in seeds:
                        actual_seed = seed + index if seed == 9141 else seed
                        pool = original.paired_positions(text, target, decoy, by_left, actual_seed)
                        encoded = original.encode(text, pool)
                        # Verify planting directly from source offsets, independently of the grouping code.
                        signature_x, signature_z = Counter(), Counter()
                        for i, j in pool:
                            assert text[i:i+2] == target and text[j:j+2] == decoy
                            signature = lambda k: (text[k-1] == ' ', text[k+2] == ' ', text[k-1] if by_left else '')
                            signature_x[signature(i)] += 1
                            signature_z[signature(j)] += 1
                        assert signature_x == signature_z
                        audit = AuditScore(encoded)
                        assert audit.count['X'] == audit.count['Z'] == len(pool)
                        incoming = sum(abs(audit.edges[s, 'X'] - audit.edges[s, 'Z']) for s in audit.symbols)
                        outgoing = sum(abs(audit.edges['X', s] - audit.edges['Z', s]) for s in audit.symbols)
                        eligible = 'X' in audit.eligible and 'Z' in audit.eligible
                        row = {'language': language, 'partition': partition, 'target': target, 'decoy': decoy,
                               'left_matched': by_left, 'seed': actual_seed, 'pairs': len(pool),
                               'eligible': eligible, 'incoming_L1': incoming, 'outgoing_L1': outgoing, 'scores': {}}
                        for version in ('literal', 'prose'):
                            x, z = audit.total(('X', *target), version), audit.total(('Z', *target), version)
                            row['scores'][version] = {'X': x, 'Z': z, 'difference_X_minus_Z': x-z}
                            if by_left:
                                assert incoming == 0 and math.isclose(x, z, abs_tol=1e-12)
                        output['seed_sensitivity'].append(row)
                        if seed == 9141:
                            label = f'{language}/{partition}/{target}-{decoy}/left={by_left}'
                            output['audited_texts'].append(verify_text(encoded, label, tracked=[('X', *target), ('Z', *target)]))
    for edition in ('zl', 'it'):
        for partition, pages in zip(('train', 'evaluation'), corpus.split_pages('practice', edition)):
            text = ' '.join(w for p in pages for ln in p.lines if ln.unit == 'P'
                            for w in ln.words if w.isascii() and w.isalpha())
            for single_loss in (0, 1):
                output['audited_texts'].append(verify_text(text, f'{edition}/{partition}/singleton={single_loss}', single_loss, original.DRAFT_TRIPLETS))
    output['independent_line_chain'] = independent_line_chain()
    (ROOT / 'audit.json').write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
    print(json.dumps({'audited_texts': len(output['audited_texts']), 'seed_conditions': len(output['seed_sensitivity'])}))


def independent_line_chain():
    """Fit a first-order table separately and emit glyphs without any pair fusion."""
    results = []
    for edition in ('zl', 'it'):
        training, evaluation = corpus.split_pages('practice', edition)
        clean = lambda pages: [' '.join(w for w in ln.words if w.isascii() and w.isalpha())
                               for p in pages for ln in p.lines if ln.unit == 'P']
        train = [ln for ln in clean(training) if ln]
        lengths = [len(ln) for ln in clean(evaluation) if ln]
        starts, transitions = Counter(ln[0] for ln in train), defaultdict(Counter)
        for line in train:
            for i in range(1, len(line)):
                transitions[line[i-1]][line[i]] += 1
        for seed in range(18710, 18716):
            rng = random.Random(seed)
            def draw(counts):
                # Sorted, cumulative integer sampling differs from the inherited expanded-list sampler.
                threshold = rng.randrange(sum(counts.values()))
                for symbol, count in sorted(counts.items()):
                    if threshold < count:
                        return symbol
                    threshold -= count
                raise AssertionError('invalid transition draw')
            lines = []
            for length in lengths:
                sequence = [draw(starts)]
                while len(sequence) < length:
                    options = transitions[sequence[-1]]
                    if len(sequence) == length - 1:
                        options = Counter({s: n for s, n in options.items() if s != ' '})
                    sequence.append(draw(options or starts))
                lines.append(''.join(sequence))
            text = ' '.join(lines)
            assert [len(s) for s in lines] == lengths and '  ' not in text
            calculator = AuditScore(text)
            row = {'edition': edition, 'seed': seed, 'characters': len(text),
                   'sha256': hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest(), 'ranks': {}}
            for version in ('literal', 'prose'):
                losses = [calculator.total(t, version) for t in product(calculator.eligible, repeat=3) if t[0] not in t[1:]]
                row['ranks'][version] = {}
                for t in original.DRAFT_TRIPLETS:
                    if not all(ch in calculator.p for ch in t):
                        continue
                    score = calculator.total(t, version)
                    rank = sum(x <= score or math.isclose(x, score, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-12) for x in losses) / len(losses)
                    row['ranks'][version]['|'.join(t)] = {'rank': rank, 'competing': all(ch in calculator.eligible for ch in t)}
            results.append(row)
    return results


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

step.json.statement: I independently reran and audited P-L1-007 on the pinned public practice/reference inputs. All recorded results reproduce exactly. Separate counting, Pearson and loss code confirms the numerical scores and the candidate cutoff decisions. Matched wrong-origin symbols can outscore genuine fusions; equal incoming contexts force ties even when outgoing contexts differ. New direct-emission line controls again yield low ligature ranks without performing symbol fusion. The q|i|e cutoff decision depends on an undefined-single-context Pearson convention. These are limitations of the statistical discriminator; they do not adjudicate physical glyph composition or decipherment.

claims_and_comparisons.attested_persian_diagram: The surviving Greater Bundahišn horoscope diagram is for chapter V A and is a different genre from a chapter II mansion list. It uses a central square and twelve peripheral houses, made by cutting four square corners diagonally. Raffaelli records the textual Cancer ascendant at nineteen degrees and associated zodiac assignments for Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, Venus and Mercury, the Sun, the Moon and the nodes. The manuscript diagrams have copying and placement discrepancies. The Iranian manuscript witnesses postdate the Voynich parchment dating interval. Their appropriate role here is an attested structural comparator and a source of conditional forecasts.
claims_and_comparisons.explicit_text_structure: The Indian and Greater texts describe twelve zodiacal constellations and twenty-eight subdividing asterisms, with four directional chieftains and a chief over them. West and Anklesaria differ in how they place Sataves and Vanand on the south and west axes. MacKenzie cautions that only twenty-seven mansion names are recoverable in the corrupt tradition. The Greater text also puts ordinary and then unmixed stars below the Moon and Sun, a potentially discriminating comparison only when objects and inside-out order are actually identifiable.
claims_and_comparisons.f67v2: Herrmann section 3.4 interprets four words around a small swirling square as sacrifice, lot, power and foundation, and proposes a possible fire context. The attribution depends on his script readings and provides no cited depiction or diagram of a particular rite. The optical check treats the proposed script values as unused.
claims_and_comparisons.f69v: Herrmann section 3.3 reports possible identifications of twenty of twenty-eight lunar mansions. His citation here is Justi's 1868 Bundehesh. He omits the identified positions and readings, so the claimed lexical correspondence cannot be reconstructed from the paper.
claims_and_comparisons.other_shared_structures: The Arabic Book of Curiosities diagram independently uses a zodiac tier and a mansion tier. The scholars' reading distinguishes twelve zodiac constellations, thirty-six other classical constellations and twenty-eight mansions. Or.133 has distinct bands including zodiac and lunar stations with differing red dot patterns. Castilian f21r uses an Arabic-derived text and a radial figurative wheel. Latin Clm 10268 f114r puts asterisms into a grid. These comparators separate writing language from the transmission history of an astronomy system.
claims_and_comparisons.zodiac: Appendix A proposes sign and month readings. Its notes acknowledge visually repeated ram and bull designs, where it tentatively assigns Capricorn and Aquarius. Unpublished lunar positions and tentative zodiac reinterpretations do not supply an objective order to impose on f69v.

extra_periodic_calendar_control.interpretation: Nadal identifies twenty-eight years of the Julian solar reckoning cycle, with pairs of dominical letters every fourth cell, plus a separate inner numerical register. This differs from a ring of twenty-eight lunar stations even though the radial count matches. The right wheel on the manuscript page uses nineteen places for the lunar golden number. These readings identify the control independently of the Voynich hypothesis.
extra_periodic_calendar_control.presentation: Add one further source-masked crop after the original panels. Render PDF physical p. 115 at 144 dpi. Crop the full figure by PDF page rectangle (65.322, 99.212, 531.104, 298.537) in points, yielding about 933×400 pixels. Take the left wheel at pixel rectangle (65,3,449,397). Its accompanying caption is omitted.
extra_periodic_calendar_control.reader_1: Twenty-eight ruled outer cells with signs and a second inner band. The first red outer entry marks a place. Using that place as index 1, taller or doubled entries recur at 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23 and 27. No heavy quadrants or brackets bind every four cells.
extra_periodic_calendar_control.reader_2: Twenty-eight outer wedges with signs, one red as a single axial distinction. No bars, scenes or dot clusters and no periodic alternation visible to this reader. The mostly red inner band has a dark entry aligned with the red outer one.

results.bundahis_sample: The TD2 figure draws a square-house horoscope with diagonal corners and twelve peripheral units. This is physically much more constrained than a round object with an arbitrary count and directly illustrates the value of a testable arrangement. It is from chapter V A, not a picture accompanying the chapter II mansion list. Its later copy and differing diagram labels warrant comparison of patterns, while an identification as the source exemplar would require independent evidence.
results.central_motif: The f67v2 crop and the wide supplement agree on a four-sided pinwheel and distinct axial and diagonal drawings. They supply no clear pedestal, bilaterally flanking figures or isolated upward flame. The known Sasanian example has a distinct raised altar and two flankers, detected despite uncertain details of the crest. This calibrates recognition of those features in one iconographic family. The difference in medium and centuries of transmission limits deductions about a highly stylized fire image.
results.layer_order: The Arabic charts visually present several separate rings, with known roles supplied independently by the manuscripts and scholarship. f69v has an inner hub and surrounding text bands, with no identified Moon or Sun ring or register for fixed asterisms. The Bundahišn layer-order prediction is therefore unscored on this figure, rather than contradicted.
repeated_units: f69v has twenty-eight repeated bars with two alternating paint and length treatments. The matched Castilian mansion wheel has twenty-eight pictorial sectors, Arabic examples have nested name, dot and zodiac tiers, and the Latin grid has twenty-eight used cells. The graphic realization of the count differs in every case. A known scheme's count is useful evidence of compatibility with a mansion reading, but lacks geographic specificity.

No independently marked twelve-supersector hierarchy or four identifiable directional leaders was resolved on f69v. The manuscript's cyclic alternation is preserved by fourteen rotations and fourteen reflections, giving twenty-eight equivalent assignments of the same pattern. Thus alternation alone cannot anchor any one named first unit or a sense of rotation.

Or.133 supplies a distinct example of visual alternation in a twelve-position band, alongside an independently divided outer mansion band. The Latin wind diagram combines a fourfold center with twelve surrounding units. Fourfold structure, concentric organization and repeated treatments recur outside the Persian text.
results.scope: Two source-masked image-model readings per crop, no literal word reading, and selected historical controls. The supported observations concern the listed views and rulings. Neither the unpublished twenty readings nor a unique route of transmission can be tested here.

visual_protocol.blinding: Randomize nine crops with seed 28067, then present two anonymous supplementary crops. Two auxiliary image-model readers receive anonymous images, a fixed structural rubric and no identifications or proposed readings. Published captions and article prose are outside the cropped diagrams. Script, media and recognizable stylistic details remain visible. Their absence of a name assignment means blinding is to supplied provenance and predictions.
visual_protocol.inference: A naked count or radial format shared with a well-identified comparator has low specificity. Identify a directional alignment only from differential markers with an independent anchor to the meaning of a direction. Identify an outside-to-inside sphere order only with evidence identifying two named layers. Zero explicit match on these structures leaves the proposed attribution unresolved. No composite similarity score or probability of origin is inferred.
visual_protocol.rubric: Record the dominant topology and visible repeating unit count, independently marked fours or twelves and their relation to the principal unit, alternation, differentiated star groups, central form and whether an upright support, rising flames, flanking people or a four-sided enclosure can be traced. Keep any uncertain count or ambiguous contour explicitly qualified. Code the supplementary f67v2 view for slender axes and separate diagonal decorated motifs.
visual_protocol.selection: Use the two named Voynich targets, an adjacent internal control, the earlier Or.133 comparator, two additional medieval mansion diagrams, one Latin non-mansion wind diagram and one definite historical altar. Use a supplementary attested Persian horoscope and a wider view of f67v2. Keep the differing purposes and media of these controls explicit.

statement: Compare the diagram structures proposed in Herrmann's Pahlavi hypothesis against dated Arabic and Western comparators and the surviving Bundahišn horoscope. Source-masked readers agree that f69v has 28 alternating bars and that f67v2 has a fourfold pinwheel. Neither supplies the distinctive spatial and iconographic correspondences needed to favor a particular tradition.

experiment.json.summary: Masked scan comparisons test the Persian cosmology proposal against Arabic and Western wheels, a Bundahishn house diagram and a known altar.

step.json.check: Repeat blind structural coding using unlabeled archive crops with prespecified features. Look for a separately identifiable zodiac tier, named directional markers, fixed-star and planetary-layer order, and an explicit support beneath upward flames. Compare a named sequence only after freezing label orders, phonetic rules and all allowed rotations or directions. A match should outperform Arabic-derived and Latin comparators as well as shuffled lists.

claims_and_comparisons.attested_persian_diagram: The surviving Greater Bundahišn horoscope diagram is for chapter V A and is a different genre from a chapter II mansion list. It uses a central square and twelve peripheral houses, made by cutting four square corners diagonally. Raffaelli records the textual Cancer ascendant at nineteen degrees and associated zodiac assignments for Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, Venus and Mercury, the Sun, the Moon and the nodes. The manuscript diagrams have copying and placement discrepancies. The Iranian manuscript witnesses postdate the Voynich parchment dating interval. Their appropriate role here is an attested structural comparator and a source of conditional forecasts.
claims_and_comparisons.explicit_text_structure: The Indian and Greater texts describe twelve zodiacal constellations and twenty-eight subdividing asterisms, with four directional chieftains and a chief over them. West and Anklesaria differ in how they place Sataves and Vanand on the south and west axes. MacKenzie cautions that only twenty-seven mansion names are recoverable in the corrupt tradition. The Greater text also puts ordinary and then unmixed stars below the Moon and Sun, a potentially discriminating comparison only when objects and inside-out order are actually identifiable.
claims_and_comparisons.f67v2: Herrmann section 3.4 interprets four words around a small swirling square as sacrifice, lot, power and foundation, and proposes a possible fire context. The attribution depends on his script readings and provides no cited depiction or diagram of a particular rite. The optical check treats the proposed script values as unused.
claims_and_comparisons.f69v: Herrmann section 3.3 reports possible identifications of twenty of twenty-eight lunar mansions. His citation here is Justi's 1868 Bundehesh. He omits the identified positions and readings, so the claimed lexical correspondence cannot be reconstructed from the paper.
claims_and_comparisons.other_shared_structures: The Arabic Book of Curiosities diagram independently uses a zodiac tier and a mansion tier. The scholars' reading distinguishes twelve zodiac constellations, thirty-six other classical constellations and twenty-eight mansions. Or.133 has distinct bands including zodiac and lunar stations with differing red dot patterns. Castilian f21r uses an Arabic-derived text and a radial figurative wheel. Latin Clm 10268 f114r puts asterisms into a grid. These comparators separate writing language from the transmission history of an astronomy system.
claims_and_comparisons.zodiac: Appendix A proposes sign and month readings. Its notes acknowledge visually repeated ram and bull designs, where it tentatively assigns Capricorn and Aquarius. Unpublished lunar positions and tentative zodiac reinterpretations do not supply an objective order to impose on f69v.

extra_periodic_calendar_control.interpretation: Nadal identifies twenty-eight years of the Julian solar reckoning cycle, with pairs of dominical letters every fourth cell, plus a separate inner numerical register. This differs from a ring of twenty-eight lunar stations even though the radial count matches. The right wheel on the manuscript page uses nineteen places for the lunar golden number. These readings identify the control independently of the Voynich hypothesis.

results.bundahis_sample: The TD2 figure draws a square-house horoscope with diagonal corners and twelve peripheral units. This is physically much more constrained than a round object with an arbitrary count and directly illustrates the value of a testable arrangement. It is from chapter V A, not a picture accompanying the chapter II mansion list. Its later copy and differing diagram labels warrant comparison of patterns, while an identification as the source exemplar would require independent evidence.
results.central_motif: The f67v2 crop and the wide supplement agree on a four-sided pinwheel and distinct axial and diagonal drawings. They supply no clear pedestal, bilaterally flanking figures or isolated upward flame. The known Sasanian example has a distinct raised altar and two flankers, detected despite uncertain details of the crest. This calibrates recognition of those features in one iconographic family. The difference in medium and centuries of transmission limits deductions about a highly stylized fire image.
results.layer_order: The Arabic charts visually present several separate rings, with known roles supplied independently by the manuscripts and scholarship. f69v has an inner hub and surrounding text bands, with no identified Moon or Sun ring or register for fixed asterisms. The Bundahišn layer-order prediction is therefore unscored on this figure, rather than contradicted.
repeated_units: f69v has twenty-eight repeated bars with two alternating paint and length treatments. The matched Castilian mansion wheel has twenty-eight pictorial sectors, Arabic examples have nested name, dot and zodiac tiers, and the Latin grid has twenty-eight used cells. The graphic realization of the count differs in every case. A known scheme's count is useful evidence of compatibility with a mansion reading, but lacks geographic specificity.

No independently marked twelve-supersector hierarchy or four identifiable directional leaders was resolved on f69v. The manuscript's cyclic alternation is preserved by fourteen rotations and fourteen reflections, giving twenty-eight equivalent assignments of the same pattern. Thus alternation alone cannot anchor any one named first unit or a sense of rotation.

Or.133 supplies a distinct example of visual alternation in a twelve-position band, alongside an independently divided outer mansion band. The Latin wind diagram combines a fourfold center with twelve surrounding units. Fourfold structure, concentric organization and repeated treatments recur outside the Persian text.
results.scope: Two source-masked image-model readings per crop, no literal word reading, and selected historical controls. The supported observations concern the listed views and rulings. Neither the unpublished twenty readings nor a unique route of transmission can be tested here.

historical_claims.note: Stolfi discusses f33v, including disk, rays and possible bracts, and objections from leaf division, apparent insertion, divided ray tips and rounded underground forms.
O’Neill 1944 says fol. 93, identified as Helianthus annuus and supported by six botanists, without listing diagnostic sunflower characters there.

Tucker and Talbert 2013 specify f93r for O’Neill’s sunflower, discuss compression of a tall plant, and propose Psacalium peltigerum separately for f33v. The latter identification is outside these coded comparisons.

Janick 2020 records that the surviving Hernández 1651 sunflower plates use substituted European images, one reversed from the 1633 Gerard edition. We do not count that illustration as an independent comparator.

method.coding: A ray is long at or above half the local disk radius, short below, absent if no distinct rays, and U if the relation is not clear. Margin or open basal notch is edge and attachment directly to a stem is sessile. Multiple means two or more visibly developed heads. All categories describe drawn structures. U means obscure, inapplicable, or not shown, with reasons below.
method.head_sampling: Top-left f33v head used as primary; upper-right scored separately as a crop sensitivity, sharing one page and artist. f93r is a distinct target. Dodoens single head and Besler largest central open head. Old World controls chosen for disk, compact head or ambiguous attachment; credits below. The right scabious crop and the water lily crop omit part of the ray perimeter. The Dodoens crop cuts some peripheral tip strokes. Retain uncertainty codes and inspect original when coverage matters.
prior_exposure: The organizer knew all sources and the original arguments before mask preparation and did not enter the independent ratings.

Four model reader instances scored separate panels, two per region. All report no previous viewing they could recall of the exact masked images or each other’s ratings. They received anonymous IDs and no identity key or literature.

The sunflower topic was inferable from the task or folder. Some readers recognized engraving, manuscript writing and sunflower-like silhouettes, and one head reader noticed the likely repeat. This was label masking with independent scoring, with incomplete provenance blinding.
The readers are model instances in one agent session, with shared model family and some general manuscript context. Four votes are not four independent botanical assessments.
method.scores: All matches use number of equal non-U categories followed by number of jointly visible categories, separately for each reader, no weighting. At least three comparisons are required for ranking; tables also retain the smaller denominators. Readers were given rubric and independent codes before seeing the source map. Sample is purposive; ranks are descriptive.
method.whole_sampling: Show full plant and the root region when present. Nymphaea shows only two separate leaf/flower shapes in the mask and cyclamen is a deliberately restricted root-only comparison. The latter cannot enter whole-plant rankings. The root systems of Dodoens and Besler, and one concealed f33v attachment, cannot be compared.

qualitative_checks.observation: Pale interior marks and inward-running veins are visible in several blades. Neither whole reader could trace a clear petiole-to-blade junction through the opaque fill. Nymphaea offers a visible marginal notch comparator; Petasites attachment was disputed between readers.

Both readers marked round enlargements attached to branches on f33v. Both coded the cropped cyclamen root U because the organ context was insufficient, and neither historical sunflower prints the root. The c. 1280–1350 Egerton MS 747 f18v (https://bl.digirati.io/images/ark:/81055/vdc_100058663074.0x00002c/canvas/c/44) also offers a round body with radiating fine strokes, but the two herbal cyclamen images may be descended from a related illustrated tradition. Root specificity remains unresolved.

Besler shows several heads with side branches and exposed pointed structures, so those characters can occur in historical sunflower illustrations. Whole readers split on whether its main stem dominates.

The pointed, continuous head has fine dots. Both head readers recorded absent outer rays and unknown ray-tip shape. Whole readers agree on one dominant upright and one head, direct-looking blade contacts, and fine root strands. They disagree on broad/narrow. There is no combined f33v/f93r score.

No taxon can be rejected reliably from this small purposive image sample. Historical images can inherit other images and visual features are correlated. Head masks and whole drawings answer different questions and cannot be combined as independent evidence. There is no held-out score and no text pairing.

qualitative_checks.description: Mattioli 1565 p.1122, named Umbilicus Veneris. The organizer observed clear interior blade dimples and underside views on the Old World navelwort plate. The two whole readers kept the corresponding f33v contact unknown. This is a supplementary unmasked illustration check without points.

detail.question: K-033-open-1; Stolfi 1998 open question about f33v. These are completed observations attached to the desk step.

features: short radiating marks around round form
root_crop_sensitivity.findings: Both readers agreed on every category. The two related cyclamen illustrations show a single outlined body with short peripheral marks and upright stems. The paired outer f33v bodies have similar peripheral marks and join laterally at a shared stem; contact at the partly clipped third body is less clear. A round outlined organ with radiating marks can occur in Old World depictions, while this sample distinguishes the number and positions of the bodies. Calendula was coded thick-axis from the whole view and fine strands from the restricted region, showing scope sensitivity at a thick stem neck.
root_crop_sensitivity.method: Two head readers independently rated a new six-panel grayscale root-only sheet after storing head results, with a separate code map. They saw no whole panels, though prior head exposure and recognizable illustration conventions could indicate the context. Dodoens and Besler cannot be rated because their plates omit the root region. Radius-like lines can be visible without proving anatomical type.

sensitivity.interpretation: Dropping disk boundary, outer ray length and silhouette retains two more specific head features. Both f33v views remain closer to the sampled Calendula than to either sunflower in this subset. Crosshatched textures can arise from different drawing conventions, so this is not a biological identification.

detail.source_coordinate_convention: Fractional boxes are xyxy fractions of source dimensions, rounded to nearest pixel before grayscale crop. Control pixel boxes are xyxy in the indicated original file frames. Controls used a first resize to fit 880×1070; the common final ceiling was 500×650, then small separate contact sheets for inspection. Rectangular fills cover external captions, numerals or portions of writing where separate from plant strokes.

detail.statement: On the sampled drawings f33v shares a bounded oval disk and projecting rays with the named sunflower prints. Both head readers distinguish their simple ray tips from the divided f33v tips, and the 1479 Calendula head matches f33v on all five coded features. Whole-plant readers agree on deeply divided f33v blades and rounded lower bodies, while both named sunflower prints show simple blades and lack a below-ground region. They leave f33v leaf insertion unknown. The separate f93r head is tapered, punctate and lacks a discrete ray fringe in these views. Its head scores are higher against the 1542 Petasites illustration than against either sunflower, although f93r has a closer whole-plant score with Dodoens. These comparisons do not establish either plant identity or a word-to-picture anchor.

experiment.json.summary: Two separately masked botanical comparisons find Old World parallels to selected head and whole-plant features on f33v and f93r.

step.json.check: Recreate the separately coded grayscale head and whole-plant masks from the source images, using the coordinates below. Have two new readers for each region apply the fixed five-feature rubric, recording missing regions and prior exposure before unmasking. Compare each folio separately to both named sunflower prints and the Old World controls using agreement counts and comparable-feature denominators. Include a close root-detail recheck and leave any anatomical contact unresolved when stroke overlap hides it.

historical_claims.note: Stolfi discusses f33v, including disk, rays and possible bracts, and objections from leaf division, apparent insertion, divided ray tips and rounded underground forms.
O’Neill 1944 says fol. 93, identified as Helianthus annuus and supported by six botanists, without listing diagnostic sunflower characters there.

Tucker and Talbert 2013 specify f93r for O’Neill’s sunflower, discuss compression of a tall plant, and propose Psacalium peltigerum separately for f33v. The latter identification is outside these coded comparisons.

Janick 2020 records that the surviving Hernández 1651 sunflower plates use substituted European images, one reversed from the 1633 Gerard edition. We do not count that illustration as an independent comparator.

method.coding: A ray is long at or above half the local disk radius, short below, absent if no distinct rays, and U if the relation is not clear. Margin or open basal notch is edge and attachment directly to a stem is sessile. Multiple means two or more visibly developed heads. All categories describe drawn structures. U means obscure, inapplicable, or not shown, with reasons below.
method.head_sampling: Top-left f33v head used as primary; upper-right scored separately as a crop sensitivity, sharing one page and artist. f93r is a distinct target. Dodoens single head and Besler largest central open head. Old World controls chosen for disk, compact head or ambiguous attachment; credits below. The right scabious crop and the water lily crop omit part of the ray perimeter. The Dodoens crop cuts some peripheral tip strokes. Retain uncertainty codes and inspect original when coverage matters.
prior_exposure: The organizer knew all sources and the original arguments before mask preparation and did not enter the independent ratings.

Four model reader instances scored separate panels, two per region. All report no previous viewing they could recall of the exact masked images or each other’s ratings. They received anonymous IDs and no identity key or literature.

The sunflower topic was inferable from the task or folder. Some readers recognized engraving, manuscript writing and sunflower-like silhouettes, and one head reader noticed the likely repeat. This was label masking with independent scoring, with incomplete provenance blinding.
The readers are model instances in one agent session, with shared model family and some general manuscript context. Four votes are not four independent botanical assessments.
method.scores: All matches use number of equal non-U categories followed by number of jointly visible categories, separately for each reader, no weighting. At least three comparisons are required for ranking; tables also retain the smaller denominators. Readers were given rubric and independent codes before seeing the source map. Sample is purposive; ranks are descriptive.
method.whole_sampling: Show full plant and the root region when present. Nymphaea shows only two separate leaf/flower shapes in the mask and cyclamen is a deliberately restricted root-only comparison. The latter cannot enter whole-plant rankings. The root systems of Dodoens and Besler, and one concealed f33v attachment, cannot be compared.

qualitative_checks.observation: Pale interior marks and inward-running veins are visible in several blades. Neither whole reader could trace a clear petiole-to-blade junction through the opaque fill. Nymphaea offers a visible marginal notch comparator; Petasites attachment was disputed between readers.

Both readers marked round enlargements attached to branches on f33v. Both coded the cropped cyclamen root U because the organ context was insufficient, and neither historical sunflower prints the root. The c. 1280–1350 Egerton MS 747 f18v (https://bl.digirati.io/images/ark:/81055/vdc_100058663074.0x00002c/canvas/c/44) also offers a round body with radiating fine strokes, but the two herbal cyclamen images may be descended from a related illustrated tradition. Root specificity remains unresolved.

Besler shows several heads with side branches and exposed pointed structures, so those characters can occur in historical sunflower illustrations. Whole readers split on whether its main stem dominates.

The pointed, continuous head has fine dots. Both head readers recorded absent outer rays and unknown ray-tip shape. Whole readers agree on one dominant upright and one head, direct-looking blade contacts, and fine root strands. They disagree on broad/narrow. There is no combined f33v/f93r score.

No taxon can be rejected reliably from this small purposive image sample. Historical images can inherit other images and visual features are correlated. Head masks and whole drawings answer different questions and cannot be combined as independent evidence. There is no held-out score and no text pairing.

qualitative_checks.description: Mattioli 1565 p.1122, named Umbilicus Veneris. The organizer observed clear interior blade dimples and underside views on the Old World navelwort plate. The two whole readers kept the corresponding f33v contact unknown. This is a supplementary unmasked illustration check without points.

step.json.question: K-033-open-1; Stolfi 1998 open question about f33v. These are completed observations attached to the desk step.

features: short radiating marks around round form
root_crop_sensitivity.findings: Both readers agreed on every category. The two related cyclamen illustrations show a single outlined body with short peripheral marks and upright stems. The paired outer f33v bodies have similar peripheral marks and join laterally at a shared stem; contact at the partly clipped third body is less clear. A round outlined organ with radiating marks can occur in Old World depictions, while this sample distinguishes the number and positions of the bodies. Calendula was coded thick-axis from the whole view and fine strands from the restricted region, showing scope sensitivity at a thick stem neck.
root_crop_sensitivity.method: Two head readers independently rated a new six-panel grayscale root-only sheet after storing head results, with a separate code map. They saw no whole panels, though prior head exposure and recognizable illustration conventions could indicate the context. Dodoens and Besler cannot be rated because their plates omit the root region. Radius-like lines can be visible without proving anatomical type.

sensitivity.interpretation: Dropping disk boundary, outer ray length and silhouette retains two more specific head features. Both f33v views remain closer to the sampled Calendula than to either sunflower in this subset. Crosshatched textures can arise from different drawing conventions, so this is not a biological identification.

step.json.source_coordinate_convention: Fractional boxes are xyxy fractions of source dimensions, rounded to nearest pixel before grayscale crop. Control pixel boxes are xyxy in the indicated original file frames. Controls used a first resize to fit 880×1070; the common final ceiling was 500×650, then small separate contact sheets for inspection. Rectangular fills cover external captions, numerals or portions of writing where separate from plant strokes.

source: Torsten Timm, How the Voynich Manuscript was created, first posted 2014, revised 2015 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6639), section 5, graphs 2–4 and appendices VI–VII. This tests the layout-matched comparative claim for altered forms. F-015 tested exact same-word recurrence and was refuted. F-021 established bounded previous-line one-edit excess against a within-page null and reported a public reference comparison without registering it. Here the token selection, lags, minimum length, and edit distance are inherited without tuning, and the explicit above-all reference comparison is the sole test. The pinned DSL uses single character insertion, deletion, or replacement on stored transliteration strings. Eligible current tokens have four earlier consecutive selected numbered lines on the same page. References are in source order within calibration blocks and poured into the exact selected word slots, with short corpora excluded. The measure is an adaptation of Timm's 20-line analysis, which allowed cross-page comparisons and used a different script representation. The above_all comparator passes ties and uses zero margin. This test is sensitive to the strongest reference and its calibration excerpts, and does not determine a cause of recurrence. Exploratory public checks are recorded below. The two successful prior attacks R-022 and R-024 show that a positive local excess of altered forms is compatible with nonlinguistic copying procedures; the present comparison does not adjudicate those procedures.
statement: In certain paragraph text, the share of current words of at least four transliteration characters that have a spelling exactly one character edit away on the previous line, minus the corresponding share four lines back, is at least the largest value for any reference corpus measured on the same selected word slots.

experiment.json.summary: Register whether previous-line one-edit variants exceed the strongest layout-matched reference, using the fixed F-021 repetition statistic.

exploratory_paragraph_null.interpretation: The edit-near result weakens when exact selected line lengths are preserved. The small sample is compatible with subtle layout effects and lower power. Matching selected line length does not fix the number of eligible long tokens across positions. Voynich grammar and the production process cannot be identified by these tests.
exploratory_paragraph_null.method: Use P paragraphs from explicit opening and ending markers. Keep contiguous interior runs of at least five certain-token lines. Exclude first and last paragraph lines. For each current eligible token record binary exact hits (minimum length 2) and one-character-edit hits (minimum length 4), previous line minus four back. Shuffle whole intact lines inside each eligible run with 199 permutations, Python Random seed 408, once unrestricted and once restricted to equal certain-token counts. One-sided p with ties counted toward the null. This is a smaller public subset with a different question from the reference comparison.

detail.statement: A tall green-stemmed plant drawing with layered coiled blade-like parts, six separate blue painted lobes at the upper right, and a rounded, lightly outlined lower body at the foot of the stem.
visual_uncertainty: The bold blue lobe count is six. Fine, unpainted lines around the small rosette do not consistently close into additional separate lobes. A fine short stalk appears to run from its underside into the upper crown, with the lower join partly hidden.

Five visible blade-like shapes are distinguishable by drawn edges, innermost notches, or stalk connections. The green and olive curved areas behind them share concealed boundaries and are grouped into one painted region. This grouping does not establish that they are one leaf.

A pale two-line stalk ends in a small loop inside the lower part of the central blade. Thin branches in the fan overlap; isolated lines were not counted as separate stalks. Five short upper-leaning stubs can be traced at least partly to the main stem, with the two thinnest brown connections less certain.

The broad lowest form is called root by position only. Its outer line is partly faint in the lower right margin. Numerous interior hooks and shorter marginal scallops are visible; their number and anatomy are uncertain.
Faint reversed or offset marks in the left background and marginal number-like marks lack visible joins to the plant. They are not assigned to the drawing. No taxon is identified.

check: Apply the same published spellings mechanically to connected lines using an explicit symbol inventory fixed in advance. Compare independently attested cognates at multiple word positions and whole paradigms with named early sources and present-day localities. Validate the comparisons by leaving whole documents or speakers out. Record word-level eligibility, alternative spellings and uncertainty. Assess extinction only after independent historical and community documentation makes a specific variety identifiable.

detail.check: Apply the same published spellings mechanically to connected lines using an explicit symbol inventory fixed in advance. Compare independently attested cognates at multiple word positions and whole paradigms with named early sources and present-day localities. Validate the comparisons by leaving whole documents or speakers out. Record word-level eligibility, alternative spellings and uncertainty.
