interpretation: Three matched editions share both reported written endings. Frequency varies by edition, and chi alone occurs in all four matched editions and in the Highland Puebla treebank.

Much of chi counting comes from a few frequent spellings. A terminal letter string can belong to unrelated stems or forms, so it does not by itself identify the proposed owl root. Counts across books preserve the same presence pattern.

Living regional varieties in the proposed areas are independently documented. The published label assays leave the manuscript’s variety unassigned and support no extinction conclusion for a specific historical speech community.

A sound correspondence supported in independently read examples at several word positions could establish affinity to groups retaining that reflex. The raw letter-sequence indicator gives a limited comparison among written editions.

lexical_checks.interpretation: The two Puebla texts share this lexical spelling. The Morelos and Isthmus editions express the noun differently.

lexical_checks.gloss_context: a stone offered instead of bread
lexical_checks.interpretation: A shared sense gives a useful comparison within a single passage. Morphological and dialect inferences require more tokens and matched grammatical forms.

lexical_checks.gloss_context: a man finds the hidden object
lexical_checks.interpretation: Here Morelos and both Puebla texts share final tl in one identifiable lexical comparison. The k/c contrast is a spelling choice in the two Puebla editions.

parallel_corpus_method.comparability: Parallel text controls much of the subject matter. Each edition has its own orthography, contributors, vocabulary and morphosyntax. The printed strings are not phonetic measurements or language genealogies. Report the Highland treebank as an unmatched genre check. The 3,755 verse-number preliminary match permitting bridged markers gave the same qualitative result. Remove bridged verses in the principal result. Historical works are independent follow-up controls, with different genres and orthographic conventions.
parallel_corpus_method.data_scope: Local descriptive comparison using publicly readable editions. Only aggregate results and a few word examples are used here. The colonial Nahuatl, modern dictionaries and nonparallel Highland sample do not enter the four-edition counts.
parallel_corpus_method.selection: All chapters of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John in four eBible HTML packages. Include a verse ID only when the displayed number is a single number equal to that ID in every edition and text remains. Remove chapter headings, navigation, section headings, references, superscript verse numbers and footnotes. Count all remaining Unicode letter/mark tokens after NFC and casefold, retaining internal apostrophes and lexical saltillo. Run a second normalization without combining marks and report type as well as token counts. Count tl, tli, tle, chi and chih as literal ending sequences, including complete tokens that match the sequence.

published_label_assay.interpretation: With printed 2013 spellings, the cactus and agave already conflict under this symbol rule. Harmonizing the final i/y permits nine partial assignments, all eliminated by the original fish reading. With the later fish reading RF1b has one assignment at four examples and predicts the fifth published spelling exactly. Some choices of ZL alternatives give two or three solutions for all five, and other choices give zero. IT2a gives zero after adding its fish reading in all tested settings. These are published examples chosen before this audit but used by the underlying authors to develop the hypothesis. A correspondence calculation on them says little about predicting a new passage or locating a dialect.
published_label_assay.location_caveat: The p.75 fish panel has the two Pisces fish and is f70v2 in the current foliation. The legacy Stolfi interlinear label list attaches the corresponding word to the central star. An exclusive relation to the fish is unresolved. The cube is f102v2 at locus 6 across the compared pinned editions.
published_label_assay.method: Use the named labels from the authors’ published argument in order cactus, agave, fish-associated, cube, paddle-shaped root. Read the exact pinned ZL3b/IT2a/RF1b locus strings. At ZL alternatives, enumerate both stated values in brackets. Split EVA with ch as one symbol and every other visible symbol in these words as a single character. For each pair in order, exhaustively enumerate all nonempty output-string prefixes for newly encountered symbols, reusing the same output whenever a symbol reappears. Allow homophones, any nonempty output length and unaligned boundaries. Compare printed spellings, a terminal i/y harmonization sensitivity, and the reported later fish reading with accent marks removed. Test the alternate cube gloss atlan separately. Counts are partial mappings satisfying constraints on these examples.

detail.relation_to_existing_work: P-L3-004 (#213) already checks the authors’ illustrative names and proposes inflectional tests. This follow-up measures the claimed final sequences against matched regional corpora and quantifies spelling dependence in a single-replacement reconstruction.

2013.authors: Arthur O. Tucker and Rexford H. Talbert
2013.note: Printed p.74 invokes written tl and chi endings and shows a fish-related reading, while p.78 proposes Morelos or Puebla for the main text. The appendix parses chi as a putative lexical root in an illustrative mixed name.

2018_fish_label.note: The precise later spelling is taken from Petersen’s quotation of p.162. The quote gives a different spelling and gloss than 2013. The enumeration is conditional on that quotation and does not adopt the blog’s dictionary interpretation.

2018_text_hypotheses.authors: Jules Janick and Arthur O. Tucker
2018_text_hypotheses.note: The public abstract says the main text remains unread and considers both a lost dialect and a mixed synthetic language.

classical_owl.note: Molina and Karttunen attest chichtli, analyzed with the noun ending tli. The exact orthographic string chi alone covers unrelated forms in the measured editions.

extinction_framework.note: A grade for intergenerational transmission depends on whether speakers remain. INALI documents named varieties and location, a separate matter from an assigned manuscript language.

historical_dialectology.author: Una Canger
historical_dialectology.note: Uses cognate correspondences and positions, including several Tlaxcala, Puebla and Morelos groupings. In some named dialects the correspondence for Classical lateral affricate is t.

historical_dialectology.author: Karen Dakin
historical_dialectology.note: Her field reports show tl in several Morelos localities and context-dependent l and final variation in Xoxocotla. Morelos is itself a dialect network.
Highland Puebla material combines speech, nonfiction and examples. Its authors describe a t correspondence for Classical tl.

mouth_of_water.note: Classical relational form atlan ends in n, with the tl sequence in the water element, independently of the proposed picture label.

detail.statement: Tucker and Talbert used final tl and chi and several names borrowed between languages to propose a central or northern Mexican dialect. Both written endings occur in all four Gospel books of the Tetelcingo Morelos, Northern Puebla and Southeastern Puebla editions examined in 3,738 matching verse numbers. The Isthmus-Mecayapan edition and Highland Puebla treebank also have chi, with zero literal final tl in these samples. Five published Voynich label examples admit a partial mapping under spelling harmonization and a revised fish reading in some transliterations. The exact 2013 readings fail the same consistency model. The available observations leave the historical variety and its speaker community undetermined.

statement: Tucker and Talbert used final tl and chi and several names borrowed between languages to propose a central or northern Mexican dialect. Both written endings occur in all four Gospel books of the Tetelcingo Morelos, Northern Puebla and Southeastern Puebla editions examined in 3,738 matching verse numbers. The Isthmus-Mecayapan edition and Highland Puebla treebank also have chi, with zero literal final tl in these samples. Five published Voynich label examples admit a partial mapping under spelling harmonization and a revised fish reading in some transliterations. The exact 2013 readings fail the same consistency model. The available observations leave the historical variety and its speaker community undetermined.

experiment.json.summary: Parallel Nahuatl corpora narrow what two proposed endings can distinguish, and several published label readings depend on spelling choices.

step.json.check: Apply the same published spellings mechanically to connected lines using an explicit symbol inventory fixed in advance. Compare independently attested cognates at multiple word positions and whole paradigms with named early sources and present-day localities. Validate the comparisons by leaving whole documents or speakers out. Record word-level eligibility, alternative spellings and uncertainty. Assess extinction only after independent historical and community documentation makes a specific variety identifiable.
interpretation: Three matched editions share both reported written endings. Frequency varies by edition, and chi alone occurs in all four matched editions and in the Highland Puebla treebank.

Much of chi counting comes from a few frequent spellings. A terminal letter string can belong to unrelated stems or forms, so it does not by itself identify the proposed owl root. Counts across books preserve the same presence pattern.

Living regional varieties in the proposed areas are independently documented. The published label assays leave the manuscript’s variety unassigned and support no extinction conclusion for a specific historical speech community.

A sound correspondence supported in independently read examples at several word positions could establish affinity to groups retaining that reflex. The raw letter-sequence indicator gives a limited comparison among written editions.

lexical_checks.interpretation: The two Puebla texts share this lexical spelling. The Morelos and Isthmus editions express the noun differently.

lexical_checks.gloss_context: a stone offered instead of bread
lexical_checks.interpretation: A shared sense gives a useful comparison within a single passage. Morphological and dialect inferences require more tokens and matched grammatical forms.

lexical_checks.gloss_context: a man finds the hidden object
lexical_checks.interpretation: Here Morelos and both Puebla texts share final tl in one identifiable lexical comparison. The k/c contrast is a spelling choice in the two Puebla editions.

parallel_corpus_method.comparability: Parallel text controls much of the subject matter. Each edition has its own orthography, contributors, vocabulary and morphosyntax. The printed strings are not phonetic measurements or language genealogies. Report the Highland treebank as an unmatched genre check. The 3,755 verse-number preliminary match permitting bridged markers gave the same qualitative result. Remove bridged verses in the principal result. Historical works are independent follow-up controls, with different genres and orthographic conventions.
parallel_corpus_method.data_scope: Local descriptive comparison using publicly readable editions. Only aggregate results and a few word examples are used here. The colonial Nahuatl, modern dictionaries and nonparallel Highland sample do not enter the four-edition counts.
parallel_corpus_method.selection: All chapters of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John in four eBible HTML packages. Include a verse ID only when the displayed number is a single number equal to that ID in every edition and text remains. Remove chapter headings, navigation, section headings, references, superscript verse numbers and footnotes. Count all remaining Unicode letter/mark tokens after NFC and casefold, retaining internal apostrophes and lexical saltillo. Run a second normalization without combining marks and report type as well as token counts. Count tl, tli, tle, chi and chih as literal ending sequences, including complete tokens that match the sequence.

published_label_assay.interpretation: With printed 2013 spellings, the cactus and agave already conflict under this symbol rule. Harmonizing the final i/y permits nine partial assignments, all eliminated by the original fish reading. With the later fish reading RF1b has one assignment at four examples and predicts the fifth published spelling exactly. Some choices of ZL alternatives give two or three solutions for all five, and other choices give zero. IT2a gives zero after adding its fish reading in all tested settings. These are published examples chosen before this audit but used by the underlying authors to develop the hypothesis. A correspondence calculation on them says little about predicting a new passage or locating a dialect.
published_label_assay.location_caveat: The p.75 fish panel has the two Pisces fish and is f70v2 in the current foliation. The legacy Stolfi interlinear label list attaches the corresponding word to the central star. An exclusive relation to the fish is unresolved. The cube is f102v2 at locus 6 across the compared pinned editions.
published_label_assay.method: Use the named labels from the authors’ published argument in order cactus, agave, fish-associated, cube, paddle-shaped root. Read the exact pinned ZL3b/IT2a/RF1b locus strings. At ZL alternatives, enumerate both stated values in brackets. Split EVA with ch as one symbol and every other visible symbol in these words as a single character. For each pair in order, exhaustively enumerate all nonempty output-string prefixes for newly encountered symbols, reusing the same output whenever a symbol reappears. Allow homophones, any nonempty output length and unaligned boundaries. Compare printed spellings, a terminal i/y harmonization sensitivity, and the reported later fish reading with accent marks removed. Test the alternate cube gloss atlan separately. Counts are partial mappings satisfying constraints on these examples.

step.json.relation_to_existing_work: P-L3-004 (#213) already checks the authors’ illustrative names and proposes inflectional tests. This follow-up measures the claimed final sequences against matched regional corpora and quantifies spelling dependence in a single-replacement reconstruction.

2013.authors: Arthur O. Tucker and Rexford H. Talbert
2013.note: Printed p.74 invokes written tl and chi endings and shows a fish-related reading, while p.78 proposes Morelos or Puebla for the main text. The appendix parses chi as a putative lexical root in an illustrative mixed name.

2018_fish_label.note: The precise later spelling is taken from Petersen’s quotation of p.162. The quote gives a different spelling and gloss than 2013. The enumeration is conditional on that quotation and does not adopt the blog’s dictionary interpretation.

2018_text_hypotheses.authors: Jules Janick and Arthur O. Tucker
2018_text_hypotheses.note: The public abstract says the main text remains unread and considers both a lost dialect and a mixed synthetic language.

classical_owl.note: Molina and Karttunen attest chichtli, analyzed with the noun ending tli. The exact orthographic string chi alone covers unrelated forms in the measured editions.

extinction_framework.note: A grade for intergenerational transmission depends on whether speakers remain. INALI documents named varieties and location, a separate matter from an assigned manuscript language.

historical_dialectology.author: Una Canger
historical_dialectology.note: Uses cognate correspondences and positions, including several Tlaxcala, Puebla and Morelos groupings. In some named dialects the correspondence for Classical lateral affricate is t.

historical_dialectology.author: Karen Dakin
historical_dialectology.note: Her field reports show tl in several Morelos localities and context-dependent l and final variation in Xoxocotla. Morelos is itself a dialect network.
Highland Puebla material combines speech, nonfiction and examples. Its authors describe a t correspondence for Classical tl.

mouth_of_water.note: Classical relational form atlan ends in n, with the tl sequence in the water element, independently of the proposed picture label.

statement: Use the project’s existing g_self_citation implementation at its default seed 2, with the public ZL practice training pages as its only input for word and glyph weights. Its initial stock is five draws from the 200 most frequent training forms, and each output copies uniformly from up to the last 40 items and makes zero, one, one or two attempts at a glyph change in EVA-basic. Replacement, insertion and deletion use the existing thresholds and learned marginal glyph frequencies. Run it on one dummy page of 1,000 rows of 12 placeholder slots, so it never resets its memory or reads an actual line number, paragraph position or page identity inside its loop. Concatenate the outputs and let the scorer put the continuous stream into the manuscript line layout. Freeze the sampler settings and use seed 2 unless rejected by screening of markers and all contiguous four-word sequences, including those spanning transport rows. Seed 2 passed the guard before any scoring of the sample. There is no edit targeting a line or its place on the page. Public controls independently permute the same stock within page, with and without fixed lengths at every slot.

public_practice.interpretation: Both page-matched controls fail, including the one holding every token length in place. The continuous ordered process passes with the same public layout. Its generated words average 15.22 transliteration characters, versus 4.92 for certain paragraph words in the public evaluation sample. The attack probes the power of this one comparator; it does not model the manuscript’s full set of properties.
public_practice.shuffle_method: Use seed 408 within the public placement. Shuffle only paragraph-token slots on each page, leaving all other slots and the unused tail untouched. For the length-matched shuffle, restrict exchanges within a page to equal transliteration character lengths. The selected page vocabularies and line lengths are preserved in both conditions.

detail.check: Recover plan.json byte-for-byte from reproduction.plan_json_bytes and both frozen scripts in one scratch directory. From the repository root on PYTHONPATH, run right_context.py calibrate, then right_context.py evaluate. Check the plan, script, calibration and evaluation digests and tables; run verify_right_context.py for the independent entropy/sampling audit. A next test should calibrate contextual and word-position conditioning on new contrasts before any manuscript use, particularly investigating the repeatable us/um reversal. All weights, cutoffs, contrasts and seed lists in this experiment remain frozen.
findings: On the primary calibration condition (exact-left matching, full matched-pool replacement), all 30 paired trials favor the genuine candidate under bilateral JS. The automatically chosen cutoff is 0.13251493881410006, with strict loss < cutoff-1e-12 acceptance. It accepts 15/30 genuine candidates and 1/30 calibration decoys. This empirical calibration count does not establish a population error rate.

With the same fixed rule on evaluation text beyond the control prefix used in P-L1-007, bilateral JS gives 24 genuine wins and 6 decoy wins across 30 repeats (six language/contrast strata, five seeds each). Its frozen cutoff accepts 14/30 genuine candidates and 0/30 decoys. Left-only JS and the inherited eight-rule prose loss each tie all 30 times and accept 5/30 candidates of each origin at their separately calibrated cutoffs.

Evaluation wins by contrast: English in/is 4/5, an/at 5/5; Latin re/ra 5/5, us/um 0/5; Italian la/le 5/5 and ra/ri 5/5. Seeds reuse the same text and are not independent language samples. The us/um reversal is stable under all five fixed seeds.

At half matched-pool replacement with exact-left matching, bilateral JS gives 26 genuine wins and 4 decoy wins; the cutoff accepts 11/30 genuine candidates and 1/30 decoys. These are secondary sensitivity results with the full-coverage calibration cutoff retained.

Matching only word-boundary positions, without equal incoming contexts, reduces full-coverage evaluation performance to 16 genuine and 14 decoy wins. The frozen bilateral cutoff accepts 8/30 genuine candidates and 0/30 decoys. This limits transfer beyond the primary matched-left design.

Matching both incoming and outgoing glyph counts forces equal left and right probability distributions for X and Z, so both JS scores tie. All 30 full-coverage evaluation trials and all 25 supported half-coverage evaluation trials behave this way. Five half-coverage trials fail the preregistered minimum support; exclusions are retained in the tables.

Under the same frozen cutoff, bilateral JS accepts no candidates among 118 scored letter/component combinations on three untouched natural streams and no candidates among 2368 combinations on sixty new first-order direct-emission streams. All sixty chains emit one glyph at a time without a fusion operation. The corresponding left-only JS cutoff accepts 45 generated-text combinations across 31 of the 60 streams; inherited eight-rule raw-loss cutoff accepts none. These finite and dependent controls do not prove a zero general false-positive rate.

A separate entropy-form implementation verifies 1440 paired JS values and 4972 negative-control JS values, with maximum absolute discrepancy 9.43689570931383e-16 and identical cutoff decisions. Independent cumulative-table sampling regenerates all sixty chain hashes; hashes of the three natural streams also match.
limitations: The evaluated objects are planted substitutions in normalized public natural text, not manuscript signs. No manuscript result or decipherment claim is made.

Six selected contrasts in three languages are the evidence units; five seeds per contrast are robustness repetitions. Training, calibration and evaluation use different blocks/windows from the same pinned books, not independent authors or genres.

The empirical negative cutoff pools thirty related calibration trials. Zero observed decoy/negative acceptances in evaluation does not bound the population false-positive rate without additional assumptions.

The new statistic uses normalized raw adjacency distributions including spaces, while the inherited score uses trimmed incidence entries. The baseline here is a separately calibrated raw loss, not the paper's original five-percent rank criterion.

Partial planting and grammar can change the residual component contexts. The stable us/um reversal and weaker word-position-only result show that adding right context does not eliminate this confounding.
All matching, support, seed, cutoff and sample-window rules were frozen publicly before their corresponding evaluation. No outcome-driven retuning was performed.

plan.eligibility: At least 40 occurrences of each engineered candidate and each proposed component A,B in the encoded text; nonempty incoming/outgoing distributions. No minimum distinct-context count. Report excluded conditions.
plan.hypothesis: Adding candidate right-context similarity to the proposed second component improves genuine-versus-decoy discrimination under matched immediate left contexts.
plan.js_definition: Equal-weight Jensen-Shannon divergence, log base 2, sum only nonzero probability terms, no smoothing, raw adjacency counts including spaces. Requires nonempty distributions; singleton distributions are valid.
plan.manuscript_gate: Do not evaluate manuscript candidate triplets in this experiment. A positive result on these selected controls would still need new language/text and scan validation.
plan.negative_controls: On untouched evaluation streams and 20 new direct-emission first-order character chains per language, score every letter C not A or B with at least 40 occurrences, using the same fixed components and cutoff. Fit chains on the first 40000 complete-word characters of refcorpus.train_text. Emit exactly 40000 glyphs from one table with sampled starts; end on a nonspace glyph. Each case has no pair-fusion operation. Report candidate-level counts and sample-level any-acceptance separately; samples/contrasts share data.
plan.paired_comparison: A genuine win means score(X,A,B) < score(Z,A,B) - 1e-12. Reverse inequality is a decoy win; otherwise tie. Report by language and contrast; seeds are robustness replicates, not independent samples.
plan.pairing: Find target AB and decoy AD in words. Match word-initial and word-final position flags. Additional modes match previous glyph (left) or previous and next glyph (both). Shuffle groups and pair lists with each fixed seed. Accept edits only when starts differ by at least 3 and are not within 2 positions of a previous accepted start. Replace the target by X and decoy by Z in one shared text.
plan.partitioning: Calibration: first 40000 characters from refcorpus.calib_text, drop final partial word. Evaluation: refcorpus.control_text beginning at character 40000, drop first partial word, take at most 40000 further characters and drop final partial word. Surround each text with a space. These control blocks follow the prefix used in the earlier audit.

scores.eight_rule_prose: Previous P-L1-007 eight-rule prose implementation, unchanged; raw loss, not its original rank percentile.

sources: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0260948
plan.stop_rule: No weight, contrast, seed, cutoff rule, sample window, support or matching change after observing outcome. Bugs require a documented amendment and a new plan hash.
plan.threshold: For each score, pool eligible calibration primary-condition decoy losses. Sort n losses; set cutoff to loss at zero-based index floor(0.05*n). Accept only loss < cutoff - 1e-12. This attains at most 5% empirical calibration decoy acceptance, allowing ties. Freeze cutoff file and its digest in the public branch before evaluating controls. If no eligible calibration negatives exist, report unavailable and do not improvise.

reproduction.instructions: Extract reproduce.py from the scripts dictionary, then from the repository root run python reproduce.py /path/to/step.json /path/to/scratch. It saves the exact embedded input bytes, runs calibration then evaluation and independent verification, and checks all six raw file hashes. Original plan/original_triplet.py and JSON outputs use Windows CRLF; the runner preserves/normalizes those line endings for byte-identical cross-platform reproduction without changing frozen measurement code or thresholds. Full negative-candidate output is recreated as evaluation.json; the submission retains all paired rows and per-negative-stream/contrast minima and accepted candidates.

scripts.reproduce.py:
"""Extract the submitted protocol and reproduce byte-identical Windows outputs.

Run from the repository root: python reproduce.py STEP_JSON SCRATCH_DIRECTORY
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

submission = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
scratch = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()
scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(scratch/'plan.json').write_bytes(submission['reproduction']['plan_json_bytes'].encode('utf-8'))
for name, script in submission['reproduction']['scripts'].items():
    (scratch/name).write_bytes(script.encode('utf-8'))
env = dict(os.environ)
env['PYTHONPATH'] = str(Path.cwd()) + os.pathsep + env.get('PYTHONPATH', '')
def digest(name):
    actual = hashlib.sha256((scratch/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    assert actual == submission['output_digests'][name], (name, actual)
for name in ('plan.json', 'right_context.py', 'original_triplet.py'):
    digest(name)
for command, output in [(['right_context.py', 'calibrate'], 'calibration.json'),
                         (['right_context.py', 'evaluate'], 'evaluation.json'),
                         (['verify_right_context.py'], 'verification.json')]:
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-X', 'utf8', str(scratch/command[0]), *command[1:]],
                   env=env, check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    # Original outputs used native Windows CRLF. Preserve their published raw hashes
    # across operating systems; the frozen measurement code is left untouched.
    path = scratch/output
    path.write_bytes(path.read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n').replace(b'\n', b'\r\n'))
    digest(output)
    print(output, 'exact digest matched', flush=True)

detail.statement: I froze a bilateral-context discriminator and its calibration cutoffs before evaluating fresh reference-text controls. The score averages Jensen-Shannon divergences between candidate/first-component left contexts and candidate/second-component right contexts. With exact left-context matching, genuine candidates beat decoys in 24/30 evaluation repeats across six contrasts; the left-only and inherited eight-rule losses tie in every repeat. The frozen bilateral cutoff accepts 14 genuine candidates and zero decoys. However, us/um fails in all five repeats, word-position-only matching gives just 16/30 genuine wins, and exact matching of both sides forces ties. This supports a conditional improvement, not a general glyph-composition test. No manuscript triplets were evaluated.

All sixty chains emit one glyph at a time without a fusion operation. The corresponding left-only JS cutoff accepts 45 generated-text combinations across 31 of the 60 streams; inherited eight-rule raw-loss cutoff accepts none. These finite and dependent controls do not prove a zero general false-positive rate.

A separate entropy-form implementation verifies 1440 paired JS values and 4972 negative-control JS values, with maximum absolute discrepancy 9.43689570931383e-16 and identical cutoff decisions. Independent cumulative-table sampling regenerates all sixty chain hashes; hashes of the three natural streams also match.
limitations: The evaluated objects are planted substitutions in normalized public natural text, not manuscript signs. No manuscript result or decipherment claim is made.

Six selected contrasts in three languages are the evidence units; five seeds per contrast are robustness repetitions. Training, calibration and evaluation use different blocks/windows from the same pinned books, not independent authors or genres.

The empirical negative cutoff pools thirty related calibration trials. Zero observed decoy/negative acceptances in evaluation does not bound the population false-positive rate without additional assumptions.

The new statistic uses normalized raw adjacency distributions including spaces, while the inherited score uses trimmed incidence entries. The baseline here is a separately calibrated raw loss, not the paper's original five-percent rank criterion.

Partial planting and grammar can change the residual component contexts. The stable us/um reversal and weaker word-position-only result show that adding right context does not eliminate this confounding.
All matching, support, seed, cutoff and sample-window rules were frozen publicly before their corresponding evaluation. No outcome-driven retuning was performed.

plan.eligibility: At least 40 occurrences of each engineered candidate and each proposed component A,B in the encoded text; nonempty incoming/outgoing distributions. No minimum distinct-context count. Report excluded conditions.
plan.hypothesis: Adding candidate right-context similarity to the proposed second component improves genuine-versus-decoy discrimination under matched immediate left contexts.
plan.js_definition: Equal-weight Jensen-Shannon divergence, log base 2, sum only nonzero probability terms, no smoothing, raw adjacency counts including spaces. Requires nonempty distributions; singleton distributions are valid.
plan.manuscript_gate: Do not evaluate manuscript candidate triplets in this experiment. A positive result on these selected controls would still need new language/text and scan validation.
plan.negative_controls: On untouched evaluation streams and 20 new direct-emission first-order character chains per language, score every letter C not A or B with at least 40 occurrences, using the same fixed components and cutoff. Fit chains on the first 40000 complete-word characters of refcorpus.train_text. Emit exactly 40000 glyphs from one table with sampled starts; end on a nonspace glyph. Each case has no pair-fusion operation. Report candidate-level counts and sample-level any-acceptance separately; samples/contrasts share data.
plan.paired_comparison: A genuine win means score(X,A,B) < score(Z,A,B) - 1e-12. Reverse inequality is a decoy win; otherwise tie. Report by language and contrast; seeds are robustness replicates, not independent samples.
plan.pairing: Find target AB and decoy AD in words. Match word-initial and word-final position flags. Additional modes match previous glyph (left) or previous and next glyph (both). Shuffle groups and pair lists with each fixed seed. Accept edits only when starts differ by at least 3 and are not within 2 positions of a previous accepted start. Replace the target by X and decoy by Z in one shared text.
plan.partitioning: Calibration: first 40000 characters from refcorpus.calib_text, drop final partial word. Evaluation: refcorpus.control_text beginning at character 40000, drop first partial word, take at most 40000 further characters and drop final partial word. Surround each text with a space. These control blocks follow the prefix used in the earlier audit.

scores.eight_rule_prose: Previous P-L1-007 eight-rule prose implementation, unchanged; raw loss, not its original rank percentile.

sources: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0260948
plan.stop_rule: No weight, contrast, seed, cutoff rule, sample window, support or matching change after observing outcome. Bugs require a documented amendment and a new plan hash.
plan.threshold: For each score, pool eligible calibration primary-condition decoy losses. Sort n losses; set cutoff to loss at zero-based index floor(0.05*n). Accept only loss < cutoff - 1e-12. This attains at most 5% empirical calibration decoy acceptance, allowing ties. Freeze cutoff file and its digest in the public branch before evaluating controls. If no eligible calibration negatives exist, report unavailable and do not improvise.

reproduction.instructions: Extract reproduce.py from the scripts dictionary, then from the repository root run python reproduce.py /path/to/step.json /path/to/scratch. It saves the exact embedded input bytes, runs calibration then evaluation and independent verification, and checks all six raw file hashes. Original plan/original_triplet.py and JSON outputs use Windows CRLF; the runner preserves/normalizes those line endings for byte-identical cross-platform reproduction without changing frozen measurement code or thresholds. Full negative-candidate output is recreated as evaluation.json; the submission retains all paired rows and per-negative-stream/contrast minima and accepted candidates.

scripts.reproduce.py:
"""Extract the submitted protocol and reproduce byte-identical Windows outputs.

Run from the repository root: python reproduce.py STEP_JSON SCRATCH_DIRECTORY
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

submission = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
scratch = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()
scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(scratch/'plan.json').write_bytes(submission['reproduction']['plan_json_bytes'].encode('utf-8'))
for name, script in submission['reproduction']['scripts'].items():
    (scratch/name).write_bytes(script.encode('utf-8'))
env = dict(os.environ)
env['PYTHONPATH'] = str(Path.cwd()) + os.pathsep + env.get('PYTHONPATH', '')
def digest(name):
    actual = hashlib.sha256((scratch/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    assert actual == submission['output_digests'][name], (name, actual)
for name in ('plan.json', 'right_context.py', 'original_triplet.py'):
    digest(name)
for command, output in [(['right_context.py', 'calibrate'], 'calibration.json'),
                         (['right_context.py', 'evaluate'], 'evaluation.json'),
                         (['verify_right_context.py'], 'verification.json')]:
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-X', 'utf8', str(scratch/command[0]), *command[1:]],
                   env=env, check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    # Original outputs used native Windows CRLF. Preserve their published raw hashes
    # across operating systems; the frozen measurement code is left untouched.
    path = scratch/output
    path.write_bytes(path.read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n').replace(b'\n', b'\r\n'))
    digest(output)
    print(output, 'exact digest matched', flush=True)

The score averages Jensen-Shannon divergences between candidate/first-component left contexts and candidate/second-component right contexts. statement: One procedure, fitted on the public practice pages only. A scribe writes a book page by page. At each word: (1) with small probability he copies the word just written or a word from the line above, varying its ending by one glyph; 6 times in 10 the variant is a shape his tables do not hold at all. When copying from the line above he prefers a source word that does not also sit four lines back. (2) Otherwise he reaches for tables of how words sit: a successor table keyed on the last glyph of the previous word, a line-opening table, and a line-ending table keyed on the last glyph of the previous line's last word; paragraph-opening first lines follow their own tables. Words he already wrote on this page are 2.5 times likelier to be written again, words from the last 15 pages somewhat likelier. (3) When no table covers the place, 9 times in 100 he writes a word of his own devising, drawn from a fitted glyph chain; otherwise the chain itself is the fallback. Tables are counts from the public pages only; no rule names a target pattern.

visual_test.method: Two model reader instances scored the same anonymous fragments independently using Y/N/U with U for a missing, obscured or unresolved feature. Reference remained visible to both. Per region and per reader report number of equal codes and number of jointly known codes. A descriptive crown ranking needs at least two comparable features. The eight local lower figures include damaged or faint shapes. Do not combine crown and root into a single anatomical claim.
outcomes: Fragment 35 shares both the broad blunt-lobed crown and the fan of fine converging stalks. Reader A also matches individual and overlapping blade traits; reader B could not reliably trace those reference traits through overlapping paint.

The spreading base on fragment 35 is pale and roughly balanced across its junction. The f35v main base is more strongly lateral and asymmetric, with groups of returning tips and a repeated array of downward branchlets. The completeness of some edges on fragment 35 remains unclear.

Fragment 33 has more visible deep recesses on individual blades than many neighboring pieces. Its overall outline and descending base give a different combination. Several lowermost controls appear faint or overlap traces, which limits how much a low match count tells us.

If crop edges or overlay interrupted a feature, the readers could mark it unknown.

statement: One general procedure — a scribe's shop — fitted on the PUBLIC CURRIER B PAGES ONLY; no rule of it mentions m or line endings. What it fits from those pages: (1) positional word tables — the successor word given the last glyph of the word before it, the words that open a line, and the words that end a line given the last glyph of the previous line's last word (paragraph-opening lines keep their own tables); (2) a glyph chain over the line (2-4 glyph history, restarted at each line start) used where no table covers the place and as the fallback; (3) the line-length distribution; (4) memory — words already written on the page are 2.5 times likelier to be written again, words from the last 15 written pages somewhat likelier; (5) copying — with small probability the scribe copies the word just written or a word from the line above (preferring a source absent four lines back), varying its ending by one glyph, 6 times in 10 landing on a shape the tables do not hold. The scribe knows where each line begins and ends; every line is written whole. All counts come from the public Currier B training pages; the hidden pages are never touched. Statistics fitted: word successor and line-position word frequencies by last glyph, glyph-transition counts, line lengths, page and recent-page word reuse. Practice split: the line-final to mid-line ratio reaches 22.1 against the line of 10, and beats the within-line shuffle null (p <= 0.01, 199 perms).

detail.statement: State of the record and what to do next. (1) Text statistics. R-028 (mtx-light), one table-and-chain procedure fitted on public pages, reproduces 18 of the 20 established facts. It misses F-021 (similar words gather on the line above) and F-022 (previous-line one-edit repetition), and both of those have fallen to targeted attacks (R-022 and R-024 on F-021, R-027 on F-022). So no established fact currently survives meaningless text, but no single procedure has yet reproduced all twenty. The decisive generator test is now narrow: one procedure, with no rule that names a target, that adds previous-line copying with small edits to a table-and-chain generator like R-028 and reaches 20 of 20. If it does, the statistical route to language is closed. If careful attempts cannot reach it, F-021 and F-022 become the strongest evidence of structure on the record. (2) Pictures. Of 50 annotations, 2 are AGREED, 16 DISAGREE and 32 are DRAFT. Kinds agree, but free-text features do not, so more annotations in the current format cannot reach AGREED. The fix is code waiting on maintainer review: the closed feature vocabulary and ring convention (PR #448) and the picture-text statistics (PR #431). Until they land, prefer the work below to new PIC-<folio> annotations. (3) Anchors. The duplicate check that refused second looks at a different anchor is fixed on main (#532), so the second look at N-005 can be resubmitted. f80r is the best-supported single folio for an external anchor: K-013-open-1 (dated medical illustrations) and P-L4-038 (clyster, flask and bathing scenes as separate tests) can both be worked from the scans and open sources now. (4) Grid. 106 cells have failed; first keys in new cells stay useful but are not the bottleneck.

detail.statement: On the matched public layout at expected hit rate 0.124, independent hits with changing page rates gave 64/64 long-band rejections with a global null and 2/64 with page centering and fixed page counts. Independent hits with changing paragraph rates and the same expected page mean gave 40/64 long-band rejections with the page-count null and 3/64 when paragraph counts were fixed on the same page statistic. At rate 0.036 and gap-copy probability 0.30, the separately declared lag-20 statistic detects recurrence in 64/64 books with a page statistic and fixed paragraph counts, and 42/64 books when the lag pairs stay within paragraph runs. The broad 11–40 band detects it in only 7/64 and 3/64 respectively. On the paired public transcriptions, the within-paragraph 1–5 average for EVA o exceeded the intact-word shuffle in both editions (ZL p = 0.01, IT p = 0.02). The EVA r lag-20 result against the same word null changed from p = 0.01 and 0.04 with page pairs to p = 0.28 and 0.33 with paragraph pairs. Eligible lag-20 pairs fell from 445 and 444 to 55 and 57. The transliterations are paired readings of the same pages.

justi_printing_audit.locus: German translation p. 4, digital PDF p. 489, Chapter II opening
justi_printing_audit.scope: Exploratory exact-repeat requirement for the literal comma-separated German printing. Allow unresolved EVA glyphs to match in place. The check does not supply Herrmann’s omitted choices or resolve how to segment the more variable Pahlavi source names.

protocol.alignments: Primary maximum over 28 rotations and both directions. Secondary scan-cue sensitivity uses clockwise starts f69v.8, f69v.9 and f69v.10 fixed by P-L4-025. It is exploratory because a ring gap need not establish the beginning of the radial roster.
protocol.extra_sensitivity: Before scoring, add a secondary full-rotation sensitivity that exchanges names only within joint classes of length and initial symbol. It preserves the earlier initial-equality result exactly. Report the number of distinct possible label assignments in each direction, including degenerate classes.
protocol.historical_normalization: Use the spelling in each named source, join multiword labels without spaces, casefold, remove accent marks, and retain alphabetic characters including written ʾ and ʿ. For the scholarly Arabic romanization, collapse th, dh, kh, sh and gh to single units. Keep prefixes, connectors and first-name editorial restorations as printed. No stripping or substitution optimized from EVA readings.
protocol.justi_audit: Check separately whether Justi’s 1868 source cited by Herrmann gives an unambiguous complete ordered 28-vector in the print. No reconstruction or inserted missing label goes into the primary three-list comparison.
protocol.nulls: Use 3,999 uniform whole-label permutations separately in the named list and the Voynich list. Exchange only labels of equal normalized length and keep undefined labels at their observed slots. Retain the same set of alignments for observed and shuffled scores. Primary combined p is the larger of the two permutation p-values. Apply Holm correction across the three sources and two paired transcriptions. Show both single-null probabilities and report three-start sensitivity separately.
protocol.prior_exposure: The prior public reports and some comparator names were already known. This plan fixes the new score before calculating any prefix alignment. Names and radial loci come from already documented editions.
sources: Anklesaria Greater Bundahishn II.2
Ragep et al. al-Muiniyya II.3[11] Arabic names in scholarly transcription
Sela et al. Henry Bate Pal.lat.1407 §5.2 table, first name per numbered row
protocol.synthetic_check: Circularly rotate/reverse a bijective relabeling of every historical list. Re-run the score at 0 percent and 2 percent independent symbol replacement with eight seeds per list and 999 null permutations per side. This checks sensitivity in an idealized prefix-preserving symbolic encoding.
protocol.targeted_check: Separately test an intact shared-head diagnostic with the three fixed clockwise starts: al-Muiniyya positions 22–25 (Saʿd), Henry Bate table positions 22–23 (Sade), and Anklesaria positions 25 and 28 (Kaht). Record the initial two EVA units of each required locus. This direct necessity only applies to a consistent prefix-preserving encoding of those particular names.
protocol.threshold: Primary score is the Pearson association across the 378 unordered pairs of sector positions between their initial runs of shared symbols in each list. Score prefix depth beyond the first unit as max(0, min(4, prefix_length) - 1), so a first-unit match alone contributes zero. Skip any pair with an uncertain Voynich label. An alignment with zero variance is uninformative.
protocol.voynich: The 28 radial loci f69v.4–31, in Zandbergen–Landini clockwise locus order. Use ZL and Takahashi as paired primary transcriptions. Keep each locus as one label, segment each written word separately with eva-basic, then concatenate its units. Exclude an uncertain label from the prefix score without moving its slot.

detail.statement: Across 56 circular alignments, shared prefixes longer than one EVA unit do not match the ordered Anklesaria, al-Tusi, or Henry Bate lists beyond the same-length permutation controls. The lowest combined primary p-value is 0.70675 before adjustment, and all six Holm-adjusted p-values are 1.0. The three clockwise scan-cued starts and the sensitivity that also fixes initial classes yield no positive score against both nulls. The chosen test detects 24/24 clean and 24/24 noisy synthetic prefix-preserving encodings of the same lists at p ≤ 0.01. The four consecutive Arabic entries sharing the three written letters سعد require a four-locus common three-unit prefix under direct grapheme substitution. Each of the 56 alignments conflicts with at least two clear units in both primary transliterations. The literal Justi Chapter II German print branches from the Greater Bundahishn list and contains consecutive Parviz entries. An exact repeated-label rule has no compatible adjacent pair in ZL or Takahashi, with one ambiguous pair in RF. The published 20 proposed Herrmann pairs are omitted in the source, leaving that proposal without a recoverable full mapping for this page.
detail.title: Repeated prefixes give no ordered f69v match in three historical mansion lists

visual_pass.exposure: The independent reader knew the chart and the established bar count. This pass coded bar and writing alignment before consulting historical names or EVA readings.
visual_pass.note: Bars alternate in two styles, including across the top. Uneven pigment and pale strokes behind the writing gave no secure additional sector boundaries or unique starting bar.

statement: Hannig's 2020 Voynich-to-Hebrew table re-transcribed from scratch out of the PDF's embedded Voynich-1.01 font (the Voynich column is PUA text, U+F0xx = the v101 letter, so no eyeballing was needed) and scored as a frozen substitution key on the gc transliteration: practice FAIL on all five criteria, savings -0.240, and the two rows that C.13 prints for <k> and <h> are pixel-identical duplicates carrying two different Hebrew values each, so the table is internally inconsistent before any scoring. The consonant map agrees letter-for-letter with fleet-corpora's reading of the same table (their held-out savings -0.260, my practice savings -0.237 for that same map), which is a clean replication of a negative result; the only difference here is that his own two-way tables read the vowel markers as matres lectionis (<i> = י, <c> = ו), which changes little (savings -0.240, coverage 0.26-0.43 against 0.36-0.48 for the null-vowel map). All five criteria fail for every vowel reading tried, and the kill tests show why: word-order-shuffled, within-word-shuffled and random-glyph decoys decode no worse than the real pages, so the key is too free to be evidence. Note for the desk: criterion (c) needs 3 confirmed anchors and the record has 1 (4 of the 5 are disputed), so no key submission can reach a full PASS until the swarm confirms anchors.

key.json.notes: Frozen table, no search. Two glyph rows in C.13 are pixel-identical duplicates of another row and give one glyph two Hebrew values: <k> is listed for both ט and ת, <h> for both ק and כ (rendered cells compared at 600 dpi: IoU 1.000). The book's own two-way tables resolve this the other way round - ט is assigned to <K> and <k>, ק to <H> and <h>, while ת is assigned only to <k> and כ only to <h> - so the exclusive value is kept: k=ת, h=כ, and ט and ק end up with no glyph of their own. Final forms are written as base letters because the pinned Hebrew corpora are normalized with finals folded (refcorpus.HEB_FINALS) and pointing removed. The vowel markers are read the way his Hebrew-to-Voynich table reads them: <i> = י (vocalic yod, also the j of the imperfect) and <c> = ו (vocalic vav, u in the middle of a word); <o>, his 'Hauptvokal, Platzhalter für Vokal', is given no Hebrew equivalent anywhere in the book and is left unmapped (a null). Also left unmapped: <*> (End-k, 'noch nicht identifiziert'), regular צ ('noch nicht identifiziert'), the ligatures <ý> and <.>, and <\>. The same table with <i> and <c> as nulls instead was also scored on the practice split; the numbers are in the experiment summary.
key.json.source: Rainer Hannig (2020), Voynich-Hebräisch: Der Weg zur Entzifferung, self-published PDF (rainer-hannig.com): the correspondence table in section C.13 and its continuations C.14-C.22, cross-checked against the two-way alphabet tables at the end of the book. The Voynich column was read out of the PDF's embedded Voynich-1.01 font (PUA U+F0xx = the ASCII code of the v101 letter), so the codes below are v101 codes and the key runs on the 'gc' transliteration.
